content.title: The Pillars of Effective API Testing
content.explanation:
**Building a Solid Foundation for Long-Term Success:**

Effective API testing isn't just about writing tests—it's about creating a sustainable testing ecosystem that grows with your application. These foundational principles guide all other best practices.

**The Five Pillars of API Test Excellence:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    API Test Excellence                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  1. Maintainability  →  Easy to update when APIs change         │
│  2. Reliability      →  Tests pass/fail for the right reasons   │
│  3. Reusability      →  Components work across multiple tests   │
│  4. Performance      →  Tests run quickly, provide fast feedback│
│  5. Clarity          →  Tests document expected behavior        │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The Cost of Poor Test Practices:**

```
Poor Practice → Consequence → Impact
───────────────────────────────────────────────
Hardcoded values → Tests break constantly → 20 hrs/week maintenance
No test organization → Can't find tests → 5 hrs/week wasted search
Missing assertions → Bugs reach production → $10K+ incident cost
No data separation → Can't reuse tests → 100s of duplicate tests
Poor error handling → False failures → Team ignores test results
```

**The ROI of Good Practices:**

| Practice | Investment | Return |
|----------|------------|--------|
| **Test Organization** | 2 hours setup | 10 hrs/month saved |
| **Data-Driven Design** | 4 hours per suite | 50% more coverage |
| **Property Usage** | 1 hour configuration | 90% less maintenance |
| **Error Handling** | 2 hours per test set | 95% fewer false failures |
| **Version Control** | 1 hour setup | Team collaboration enabled |

**Key Mindset Shifts:**

✅ **Tests as Code:** Treat test scripts with same rigor as production code
✅ **Design for Change:** APIs will evolve—design tests that adapt
✅ **Fail Fast:** Catch issues early, fail clearly
✅ **Continuous Improvement:** Regularly refactor and improve tests
✅ **Documentation through Tests:** Tests should explain expected behavior

**The Golden Rules:**

1. **One test, one concept** - Each test should verify one thing
2. **No hardcoding** - Every value should come from a property or data source
3. **Tests are independent** - No test depends on another
4. **Clean up after yourself** - Leave the system as you found it
5. **Assert what matters** - Validate business rules, not just status codes
6. **Name clearly** - Test names explain purpose
7. **Keep it simple** - Avoid unnecessary complexity

content.title: Scalable Test Organization Strategies
content.explanation:
**Structuring Tests for Growth and Maintainability:**

As your API grows, so will your test suite. Proper organization is the difference between a maintainable asset and an unmanageable liability.

**1. Project Structure by Domain:**

```
E-commerce API Test Suite
├── User Management
│   ├── Registration
│   ├── Authentication
│   ├── Profile Management
│   └── Account Deletion
├── Product Catalog
│   ├── Product Listing
│   ├── Product Search
│   ├── Product Details
│   └── Category Management
├── Shopping Cart
│   ├── Add to Cart
│   ├── Update Cart
│   ├── Remove from Cart
│   └── Cart Checkout
├── Order Processing
│   ├── Create Order
│   ├── Order Status
│   ├── Order History
│   └── Order Cancellation
└── Payment
    ├── Payment Methods
    ├── Process Payment
    └── Refund
```

**2. Test Suite Organization by Type:**

```
API Test Suite
├── Smoke Tests (Critical Path)
│   ├── Health Check
│   ├── Authentication
│   └── Basic CRUD
├── Functional Tests (Feature Complete)
│   ├── User Flows
│   ├── Product Flows
│   └── Order Flows
├── Regression Tests (Comprehensive)
│   ├── All Endpoints
│   ├── All Parameters
│   └── Edge Cases
├── Integration Tests
│   ├── Third-party APIs
│   ├── Database Integration
│   └── Message Queues
├── Performance Tests
│   ├── Load Tests
│   ├── Stress Tests
│   └── Endurance Tests
└── Security Tests
    ├── Authentication
    ├── Authorization
    ├── Injection
    └── Data Exposure
```

**3. Naming Conventions:**

```
✅ Good Test Names:
TC001_User_Register_ValidData
TC002_User_Register_DuplicateEmail
TC003_User_Login_ValidCredentials
TC004_User_Login_WrongPassword
TC005_Product_Get_ExistingID
TC006_Product_Get_NonExistentID

❌ Bad Test Names:
Test1
NewTest
CopyOfTest
TestFinal
TestFinal2
```

**4. Test Case Template:**

```xml
<testCase name="TCXXX_Feature_Scenario">
  <description>
    [Brief description of what this test verifies]
    
    Preconditions:
    - [List any prerequisites]
    - [Environment setup required]
    
    Test Data:
    - Input: [key=value]
    - Expected: [key=value]
    
    Tags: @smoke @regression @critical
    Author: [Name]
    Created: [Date]
    Last Updated: [Date]
  </description>
  
  <properties>
    <!-- Test-specific properties with defaults -->
    <property name="testDataId" value="default-001"/>
    <property name="retryCount" value="3"/>
  </properties>
  
  <setupScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Initialize test data
      // Log test start
      log.info "Starting test: ${testRunner.testCase.name}"
    ]]>
  </setupScript>
  
  <!-- Test steps go here -->
  
  <tearDownScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Clean up test data
      // Log test result
      log.info "Test completed: ${testRunner.status}"
    ]]>
  </tearDownScript>
</testCase>
```

**5. Folder Organization in Navigator:**

```
Project: "E-commerce API"
├── [01] Smoke Tests
│   ├── TC001_HealthCheck
│   └── TC002_Auth_Login
├── [02] User Management
│   ├── TC010_Register
│   ├── TC011_Login
│   └── TC012_Profile
├── [03] Product Catalog
│   ├── TC020_ListProducts
│   ├── TC021_SearchProducts
│   └── TC022_ProductDetails
├── [04] Order Processing
│   ├── TC030_CreateOrder
│   ├── TC031_GetOrder
│   └── TC032_CancelOrder
├── [05] Data
│   ├── test-users.csv
│   ├── test-products.csv
│   └── test-orders.csv
└── [06] Scripts
    ├── CommonUtilities.groovy
    ├── DataGenerators.groovy
    └── AssertionHelpers.groovy
```

**6. Test Grouping with Tags:**

```xml
<testCase name="TC001_User_Register">
  <tags>
    <tag>smoke</tag>
    <tag>user</tag>
    <tag>critical</tag>
    <tag>regression</tag>
  </tags>
</testCase>

<!-- Run only smoke tests -->
testrunner.sh -T smoke project.xml

<!-- Run all except slow tests -->
testrunner.sh -X slow project.xml
```

**7. Shared Test Components:**

```xml
<!-- Reusable authentication test step -->
<testStep name="Authenticate" type="restrequest">
  <config>
    <endpoint>${#Project#authUrl}/login</endpoint>
    <method>POST</method>
    <request>
      <![CDATA[
      {
        "username": "${username}",
        "password": "${password}"
      }
      ]]>
    </request>
  </config>
  
  <!-- Export token to context -->
  <script>
    <![CDATA[
      def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(messageExchange.responseContent)
      context.setProperty('authToken', json.token)
    ]]>
  </script>
</testStep>

<!-- Reuse in multiple test cases -->
<testStep name="Authenticate" type="call" testStep="Common.Authenticate"/>
```

**8. Test Documentation Standards:**

```xml
<testCase name="TC023_Order_CalculateTax">
  <description>
    Verify tax calculation for orders based on location
    
    Business Rules:
    - US orders: 8% tax
    - EU orders: 20% VAT
    - Other countries: 0% tax
    
    Test Scenarios:
    1. US address → 8% tax
    2. UK address → 20% tax
    3. Japan address → 0% tax
    
    Dependencies:
    - User must be authenticated
    - Products must be in cart
    
    Expected Results:
    - Tax amount matches rule
    - Total = subtotal + tax
    - Response includes tax breakdown
  </description>
</testCase>
```

**9. Organization Anti-Patterns:**

❌ **Monolithic Test Cases:** Testing too much in one test
❌ **Inconsistent Naming:** Random names that don't explain purpose
❌ **Deep Nesting:** Too many folder levels (max 3-4)
❌ **Orphaned Tests:** Tests with no clear owner
❌ **Duplicate Tests:** Same logic copied multiple times
❌ **Dead Tests:** Tests that are never run

**10. Organization Checklist:**

✅ Clear, consistent naming convention
✅ Logical grouping by feature/module
✅ Tags for filtering and categorization
✅ Documentation in test descriptions
✅ Shared components extracted
✅ Properties for configuration
✅ Clean separation of test data
✅ Regular review and cleanup

content.title: Using External Data Sources for Data-Driven Testing
Mastering Data-Driven Testing
content.explanation:
**Separating Test Logic from Test Data for Maximum Coverage:**

Data-driven testing is the practice of running the same test logic with multiple sets of input data. This is one of the most powerful techniques for achieving comprehensive test coverage with minimal maintenance.

**Why Data-Driven Testing Matters:**

```
Without Data-Driven Testing:
Test A: username=user1, password=pass1
Test B: username=user2, password=pass2 (duplicate code)
Test C: username=user3, password=pass3 (more duplication)

With Data-Driven Testing:
One test + CSV with 1000 rows = 1000 test cases!
```

**1. Choosing the Right Data Source:**

| Data Source | Best For | Pros | Cons |
|-------------|----------|------|------|
| **CSV** | Simple test data, small to medium datasets | Human-readable, version-control friendly | Limited formatting, no formulas |
| **Excel** | Complex data, calculations, multiple sheets | Formulas, formatting, multiple sheets | Binary, harder to diff |
| **Database** | Large datasets, production-like data | Live data, relationships | Setup complexity, slower |
| **Grid** | Small, manual test sets | Quick, no external files | Not reusable |
| **Groovy** | Generated data, dynamic values | Flexible, no files | Harder to maintain |

**2. CSV Data Source Best Practices:**

```csv
# GOOD: Clear headers, consistent data
test_id,username,password,email,expected_status,expected_message
001,valid_user,Pass123,valid@test.com,200,Login successful
002,invalid_user,WrongPass,invalid@test.com,401,Invalid credentials
003,empty_pass,user3,,400,Password required
004,sql_injection,"' OR '1'='1",,400,Security violation

# Include edge cases
005,very_long_username_that_exceeds_normal_limits_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz,Pass123,long@test.com,400,Username too long
006,special_chars,!@#$%^&*(),special@test.com,400,Invalid characters
007,unicode_user,密码123,unicode@test.com,200,Login successful
```

**3. Excel Data Source Configuration:**

```xml
<dataSource>
  <type>Excel</type>
  <name>Test Data</name>
  <file>${projectDir}/data/test-data.xlsx</file>
  <sheet>LoginTests</sheet>
  <firstRow>header</firstRow>
  
  <!-- Named ranges for better organization -->
  <range>LoginTestData</range>
</dataSource>
```

**4. Database Data Source Pattern:**

```xml
<dataSource>
  <type>JDBC</type>
  <name>LiveTestData</name>
  <driver>com.mysql.jdbc.Driver</driver>
  <connection>jdbc:mysql://${#Project#dbHost}:3306/testdb</connection>
  <username>${#Project#dbUser}</username>
  <password>${#Project#dbPassword}</password>
  <query>
    SELECT u.username, u.email, c.country, c.tax_rate
    FROM test_users u
    JOIN countries c ON u.country_id = c.id
    WHERE u.active = 1
    LIMIT 100
  </query>
</dataSource>
```

**5. Data Generation with Groovy:**

```groovy
// Generate realistic test data programmatically
import groovy.json.JsonOutput

class TestDataGenerator {
    def random = new Random()
    
    def generateUser() {
        def id = random.nextInt(10000)
        def firstNames = ['John', 'Jane', 'Bob', 'Alice', 'Charlie']
        def lastNames = ['Smith', 'Johnson', 'Williams', 'Brown', 'Jones']
        def domains = ['example.com', 'test.com', 'demo.org']
        
        def firstName = firstNames[random.nextInt(firstNames.size())]
        def lastName = lastNames[random.nextInt(lastNames.size())]
        def username = (firstName + lastName + id).toLowerCase()
        
        return [
            test_id: id,
            username: username,
            firstName: firstName,
            lastName: lastName,
            email: "${username}@${domains[random.nextInt(domains.size())]}",
            age: 18 + random.nextInt(50),
            country: ['US', 'UK', 'CA', 'AU', 'DE'][random.nextInt(5)],
            expected_status: 200
        ]
    }
    
    def generateCSV(count) {
        def csv = "test_id,username,firstName,lastName,email,age,country,expected_status\n"
        count.times { i ->
            def user = generateUser()
            csv += "${user.test_id},${user.username},${user.firstName},${user.lastName},${user.email},${user.age},${user.country},${user.expected_status}\n"
        }
        return csv
    }
}

def generator = new TestDataGenerator()
def csvData = generator.generateCSV(100)
new File(context.expand('${projectDir}') + '/data/generated-users.csv').write(csvData)
log.info "Generated 100 test users"
```

**6. Data-Driven Test Pattern:**

```xml
<testCase name="Data-Driven Login Test">
  <!-- Data Source -->
  <dataSource>
    <type>CSV</type>
    <file>${projectDir}/data/login-test-data.csv</file>
    <firstRow>header</firstRow>
  </dataSource>
  
  <!-- Data Source Loop -->
  <dataSourceLoop>
    <testSteps>
      <!-- Test Step 1: Login Request -->
      <testStep name="Login Request" type="restrequest">
        <config>
          <endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/auth/login</endpoint>
          <method>POST</method>
          <request>
            <![CDATA[
            {
              "username": "${username}",
              "password": "${password}"
            }
            ]]>
          </request>
        </config>
      </testStep>
      
      <!-- Test Step 2: Verify Response -->
      <testStep name="Verify Response" type="groovy">
        <script>
          <![CDATA[
            import groovy.json.JsonSlurper
            
            def loginStep = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("Login Request")
            def status = loginStep.getPropertyValue("httpResponseCode").toInteger()
            def expectedStatus = context.expand('${expected_status}').toInteger()
            def response = loginStep.getPropertyValue("response")
            
            // Log test progress
            log.info "Testing: ${context.expand('${username}')}"
            log.info "Expected: ${expectedStatus}, Actual: ${status}"
            
            // Assert status code
            assert status == expectedStatus : 
                "Row ${context.currentRow}: Expected ${expectedStatus} but got ${status}"
            
            // Additional assertions based on expected outcome
            if (status == 200) {
                def json = new JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
                assert json.token != null : "No token returned"
                assert json.user.username == context.expand('${username}') : "Username mismatch"
            } else if (status == 401) {
                assert response.contains("Invalid credentials") : 
                    "Expected error message not found"
            }
          ]]>
        </script>
      </testStep>
    </testSteps>
  </dataSourceLoop>
  
  <!-- Teardown - Report summary -->
  <tearDownScript>
    <![CDATA[
      def totalRows = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName('dataSource').getRowCount()
      def results = testRunner.results
      def passed = results.count { it.status.toString() == 'PASSED' }
      def failed = results.count { it.status.toString() == 'FAILED' }
      
      log.info "=== Data-Driven Test Summary ==="
      log.info "Total rows: ${totalRows}"
      log.info "Passed: ${passed}"
      log.info "Failed: ${failed}"
      log.info "Pass rate: ${(passed/totalRows*100).round(2)}%"
    ]]>
  </tearDownScript>
</testCase>
```

**7. Advanced Data-Driven Patterns:**

**Conditional Data Execution:**

```xml
<dataSourceLoop>
  <!-- Skip rows based on condition -->
  <condition>${run_mode} == 'full' || ${priority} == 'high'</condition>
  <testSteps>
    <!-- Test steps -->
  </testSteps>
</dataSourceLoop>
```

**Data Transformation:**

```groovy
// Transform data before use
def rawData = context.expand('${raw_data}')
def transformed = rawData.toUpperCase()
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('processed_data', transformed)
```

**Data Masking for Sensitive Info:**

```groovy
// Mask sensitive data in logs
def maskSensitive(value) {
    if (value.length() > 4) {
        return '*' * (value.length() - 4) + value[-4..-1]
    }
    return '****'
}

log.info "Processing user: ${maskSensitive(username)}"
```

**8. Data-Driven Testing Best Practices:**

✅ **Keep Data Realistic:** Use production-like data patterns
✅ **Include Edge Cases:** Empty, null, boundary, invalid
✅ **Version Control Data:** Store CSV files with test code
✅ **Document Data:** Comment on what each column represents
✅ **Start Small:** Begin with few rows, scale up
✅ **Validate Data First:** Check CSV format before running
✅ **Monitor Performance:** Large datasets may need optimization
✅ **Use Meaningful Names:** Column names should be self-explanatory
✅ **Separate by Environment:** Dev, staging, production data files
✅ **Regular Refresh:** Update test data periodically

**9. Data-Driven Testing Anti-Patterns:**

❌ **Too Much Data:** 10,000 rows when 100 would suffice
❌ **No Headers:** CSV without column names
❌ **Hardcoded Paths:** Using absolute file paths
❌ **Missing Edge Cases:** Only testing happy path
❌ **Stale Data:** Using data that no longer matches schema
❌ **No Validation:** Assuming data is correct
❌ **Poor Performance:** Database queries with no indexes

**10. Data-Driven Testing Checklist:**

✅ Column headers clear and consistent
✅ All data types match API expectations
✅ Edge cases included (nulls, boundaries)
✅ File paths use properties, not hardcoded
✅ Data validated before test execution
✅ Results tracked per data row
✅ Performance acceptable for dataset size
✅ Data files in version control
✅ Documentation for each column
✅ Regular data refresh schedule

content.title: Handling Dynamic Data with Property Transfer
Mastering Dynamic Data Management
content.explanation:
**Extracting and Reusing Dynamic Values Across Test Steps:**

Real-world APIs return dynamic data—IDs, timestamps, tokens—that must be captured and used in subsequent requests. Property transfer is the mechanism for handling this.

**Why Property Transfer Matters:**

```
Without Property Transfer:
Step 1: Create user → returns ID=12345
Step 2: Get user → must hardcode ID (impossible)
Test fails because ID is dynamic

With Property Transfer:
Step 1: Create user → returns ID=12345
     ↓ Property Transfer extracts ID
Step 2: Get user → uses ${userId} property
Test passes with any generated ID
```

**1. Property Transfer Configuration:**

```xml
<testStep name="Extract User ID" type="transfer">
  <transfers>
    <!-- Transfer from response to property -->
    <transfer>
      <source type="response" step="Create User">
        <path>$.id</path>
      </source>
      <target type="property">
        <name>userId</name>
        <targetStep>Get User</targetStep>
      </target>
    </transfer>
    
    <!-- Transfer from header to property -->
    <transfer>
      <source type="responseHeader" step="Login">
        <header>Authorization</header>
      </source>
      <target type="property">
        <name>authToken</name>
      </target>
    </transfer>
  </transfers>
</testStep>
```

**2. XPath Transfer for SOAP:**

```xml
<transfer>
  <source type="response" step="Add Numbers">
    <xpath>
      declare namespace tem='http://tempuri.org/';
      //tem:AddResult
    </xpath>
  </source>
  <target type="property">
    <name>additionResult</name>
  </target>
</transfer>
```

**3. JSONPath Transfer for REST:**

```xml
<transfer>
  <source type="response" step="Create User">
    <path>$.user.id</path>
  </source>
  <target type="property">
    <name>userId</name>
  </target>
</transfer>

<!-- Extract multiple values -->
<transfer>
  <source type="response" step="Get Users">
    <path>$.users[*].id</path>
  </source>
  <target type="property">
    <name>userIds</name>
  </target>
</transfer>
```

**4. Regex Transfer for Text Responses:**

```xml
<transfer>
  <source type="response" step="Get Token">
    <regex>token=([a-f0-9]{32})</regex>
    <group>1</group>
  </source>
  <target type="property">
    <name>sessionToken</name>
  </target>
</transfer>
```

**5. Script-Based Extraction:**

```groovy
// Groovy script for complex extraction
def response = messageExchange.responseContent
def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)

// Extract nested value
def userId = json.data.user.profile.id

// Extract with transformation
def timestamp = json.createdAt
formattedTime = new Date(timestamp).format("yyyy-MM-dd")

// Extract conditional value
def status = json.status
if (status == 'success') {
    context.setProperty('result', json.data.value)
} else {
    context.setProperty('result', json.error.message)
}

// Extract multiple values
def ids = json.items.collect { it.id }.join(',')
context.setProperty('itemIds', ids)
```

**6. Property Transfer Patterns:**

**Chained Transfers:**
```xml
<testStep name="Create User"/>
<testStep name="Extract User ID"/>
<testStep name="Create Order" using ${userId}/>
<testStep name="Extract Order ID"/>
<testStep name="Get Order" using ${orderId}/>
```

**Conditional Transfer:**
```groovy
// Only transfer if condition met
if (messageExchange.responseHeaders['#status#'][0] == '200') {
    def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(messageExchange.responseContent)
    context.setProperty('userId', json.id)
}
```

**Default Values:**
```groovy
// Provide default if extraction fails
def userId = json?.id ?: 'default-user-id'
context.setProperty('userId', userId)
```

**7. Property Scopes:**

```groovy
// Project scope - available across entire project
project.setPropertyValue('apiVersion', 'v2')

// TestSuite scope - available within suite
testSuite.setPropertyValue('environment', 'staging')

// TestCase scope - available within test case
testRunner.testCase.setPropertyValue('userId', '123')

// Context scope - available within current run
context.setProperty('temporary', 'value')

// Usage in requests
<endpoint>${#Project#apiUrl}/${#TestSuite#apiVersion}/users/${#TestCase#userId}</endpoint>
```

**8. Property Transfer Best Practices:**

✅ **Name Clearly:** Use descriptive property names (userId, not id)
✅ **Scope Appropriately:** Use smallest scope needed
✅ **Handle Failures:** Provide defaults or handle missing values
✅ **Document Dependencies:** Note which properties are required
✅ **Clean Up:** Remove temporary properties after use
✅ **Use Constants:** Store unchanging values as properties
✅ **Validate After Transfer:** Verify property was set correctly

**9. Complete Property Transfer Example:**

```xml
<testCase name="Complete User Order Flow">
  <properties>
    <property name="baseUrl" value="${#Project#apiUrl}"/>
    <property name="authToken" value=""/>
    <property name="userId" value=""/>
    <property name="orderId" value=""/>
  </properties>
  
  <testSteps>
    <!-- Step 1: Login -->
    <testStep name="Login" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${baseUrl}/auth/login</endpoint>
        <request>{"username":"test","password":"test"}</request>
      </config>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 2: Extract Token -->
    <testStep name="Extract Token" type="transfer">
      <transfers>
        <transfer>
          <source type="response" step="Login">
            <path>$.token</path>
          </source>
          <target type="property">
            <name>authToken</name>
          </target>
        </transfer>
      </transfers>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 3: Create User -->
    <testStep name="Create User" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${baseUrl}/users</endpoint>
        <headers>
          <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
        </headers>
        <request>{"name":"Test User"}</request>
      </config>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 4: Extract User ID -->
    <testStep name="Extract User ID" type="transfer">
      <transfers>
        <transfer>
          <source type="response" step="Create User">
            <path>$.id</path>
          </source>
          <target type="property">
            <name>userId</name>
          </target>
        </transfer>
      </transfers>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 5: Create Order (using userId) -->
    <testStep name="Create Order" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${baseUrl}/users/${userId}/orders</endpoint>
        <headers>
          <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
        </headers>
      </config>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 6: Extract Order ID -->
    <testStep name="Extract Order ID" type="transfer">
      <transfers>
        <transfer>
          <source type="response" step="Create Order">
            <path>$.id</path>
          </source>
          <target type="property">
            <name>orderId</name>
          </target>
        </transfer>
      </transfers>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 7: Get Order (using orderId) -->
    <testStep name="Get Order" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${baseUrl}/orders/${orderId}</endpoint>
        <headers>
          <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
        </headers>
      </config>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 8: Verify Order -->
    <testStep name="Verify Order" type="groovy">
      <script>
        <![CDATA[
          def response = messageExchange.responseContent
          def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
          
          assert json.id == context.expand('${orderId}').toInteger()
          assert json.userId == context.expand('${userId}').toInteger()
          
          log.info "Order verification passed: ${json.id}"
        ]]>
      </script>
    </testStep>
  </testSteps>
</testCase>
```

**10. Property Transfer Troubleshooting:**

| Issue | Symptom | Solution |
|-------|---------|----------|
| **Property not set** | ${property} appears literally | Check path/XPath, step executed? |
| **Wrong value** | Assertion fails with wrong value | Verify extraction path, check for transformations |
| **Scope issue** | Property not available in next step | Use correct scope (TestCase vs Context) |
| **Null value** | Property is null | Add null check, provide default |
| **Multiple matches** | First value only extracted | Use index or collect all |
| **Performance** | Property transfer slow | Optimize XPath/JSONPath, use simple paths |

**11. Property Transfer Checklist:**

✅ Source step executed before transfer
✅ Path/XPath correctly targets desired value
✅ Target property name is unique and meaningful
✅ Property scope appropriate for usage
✅ Default values for optional properties
✅ Error handling for missing values
✅ Documentation of property dependencies
✅ Cleanup of temporary properties
✅ Validation after transfer

content.title: Performance Optimization Strategies
content.explanation:
**Making Your Tests Run Faster Without Sacrificing Quality:**

Test execution time directly impacts developer productivity and feedback cycles. Slow tests lead to skipped tests and delayed feedback.

**The Cost of Slow Tests:**

```
100 tests @ 30 seconds each = 50 minutes
100 tests @ 3 seconds each = 5 minutes

Daily savings: 45 minutes
Weekly savings: 3.75 hours
Monthly savings: 15 hours
Yearly savings: 180 hours (over 4 work weeks!)
```

**1. Parallel Test Execution:**

```xml
<!-- Run test cases in parallel -->
<testSuite name="Parallel Tests" parallel="true">
  <threadCount>5</threadCount>
  <testCase name="Test 1"/>
  <testCase name="Test 2"/>
  <testCase name="Test 3"/>
  <testCase name="Test 4"/>
  <testCase name="Test 5"/>
</testSuite>

<!-- Run test steps in parallel -->
<testCase name="Parallel Steps" parallelSteps="true">
  <threadCount>3</threadCount>
  <testStep name="Independent Step 1"/>
  <testStep name="Independent Step 2"/>
  <testStep name="Independent Step 3"/>
</testCase>
```

**2. Selective Test Execution:**

```bash
# Run only smoke tests (fast)
testrunner.sh -T smoke project.xml

# Run only tests changed since last commit
# (Use with Git to identify changed tests)
git diff --name-only HEAD~1 | grep '.xml' | xargs testrunner.sh

# Run tests by priority
testrunner.sh -P priority=high project.xml
```

**3. Test Data Optimization:**

```xml
<!-- Use smaller datasets for quick feedback -->
<dataSource>
  <type>CSV</type>
  <file>${projectDir}/data/test-data.csv</file>
  <maxIterations>50</maxIterations>  <!-- Limit rows for quick runs -->
</dataSource>

<!-- Use different datasets for different environments -->
<dataSource>
  <type>CSV</type>
  <file>${projectDir}/data/${#Project#env}-test-data.csv</file>
</dataSource>
```

**4. Assertion Optimization:**

```xml
<!-- Order assertions by speed (fastest first) -->
<assertions>
  <!-- Fast: status code (single integer comparison) -->
  <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
  
  <!-- Medium: header check (string comparison) -->
  <assertion type="Response Headers"><header>Content-Type</header><value>application/json</value></assertion>
  
  <!-- Slower: JSONPath (parsing required) -->
  <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.id</path></assertion>
  
  <!-- Slowest: script assertion (full parsing + logic) -->
  <assertion type="Script"><script>...</script></assertion>
</assertions>
```

**5. Connection and Timeout Optimization:**

```xml
<!-- Optimize HTTP settings -->
<soapui-settings>
  <http>
    <!-- Keep connections alive -->
    <enableKeepAlive>true</enableKeepAlive>
    
    <!-- Reduce timeouts for faster failure detection -->
    <connectionTimeout>5000</connectionTimeout>
    <responseTimeout>10000</responseTimeout>
    
    <!-- Reuse connections -->
    <maxConnections>100</maxConnections>
  </http>
</soapui-settings>
```

**6. Memory Optimization:**

```bash
# soapui.vmoptions - Increase heap for large test suites
-Xms1024m
-Xmx4096m
-XX:+UseG1GC
-XX:+UseStringDeduplication

# Disable UI features for headless execution
-Dsoapui.jxbrowser.disable=true
-Dsoapui.scripting.debug=false
```

**7. Caching Strategies:**

```groovy
// Cache authentication tokens to avoid repeated logins
def getAuthToken() {
    def token = context.getProperty('cachedToken')
    def expiry = context.getProperty('tokenExpiry')
    
    if (token && expiry && Long.parseLong(expiry) > System.currentTimeMillis()) {
        log.info "Using cached token"
        return token
    }
    
    log.info "Getting new token"
    // Perform login and get new token
    def newToken = performLogin()
    
    context.setProperty('cachedToken', newToken)
    context.setProperty('tokenExpiry', (System.currentTimeMillis() + 3600000).toString())
    
    return newToken
}

// Cache test data to avoid repeated database queries
def testData = context.getProperty('cachedTestData')
if (!testData) {
    testData = loadTestDataFromDatabase()
    context.setProperty('cachedTestData', testData)
}
```

**8. Execution Profile Management:**

```xml
<!-- Quick smoke test profile -->
<testSuite name="Smoke Tests" runMode="SEQUENTIAL">
  <tags>
    <tag>smoke</tag>
  </tags>
</testSuite>

<!-- Comprehensive regression profile -->
<testSuite name="Full Regression" runMode="PARALLEL">
  <threadCount>10</threadCount>
  <testCase name="All Tests"/>
</testSuite>
```

**9. Performance Monitoring:**

```groovy
// Track test execution times
def metrics = [:]

testRunner.results.each { result ->
    def testName = result.testCase.name
    def time = result.timeTaken
    
    if (!metrics[testName]) {
        metrics[testName] = []
    }
    metrics[testName] << time
}

// Identify slow tests
def slowTests = []
metrics.each { test, times ->
    def avg = times.sum() / times.size()
    if (avg > 2000) {
        slowTests << [name: test, avg: avg]
    }
}

if (slowTests) {
    log.warn "Slow tests detected:"
    slowTests.sort { -it.avg }.each { test ->
        log.warn "  ${test.name}: ${test.avg.round()}ms average"
    }
}
```

**10. Optimization Best Practices:**

✅ **Profile First:** Identify actual bottlenecks before optimizing
✅ **Start Fast:** Run smoke tests immediately, full suite later
✅ **Parallelize Wisely:** Don't overload shared resources
✅ **Cache Aggressively:** Token, test data, connections
✅ **Fail Fast:** Quick assertions before slow ones
✅ **Use Headless:** Run in non-GUI mode for CI/CD
✅ **Right-Size Data:** Use minimal datasets for quick runs
✅ **Monitor Trends:** Track execution times over time

**11. Optimization Anti-Patterns:**

❌ **Premature Optimization:** Optimizing before measuring
❌ **Over-Parallelization:** Too many threads causing contention
❌ **Ignoring Setup/Teardown:** Not accounting for overhead
❌ **Caching Without Expiry:** Using stale data
❌ **Too Many Assertions:** Testing irrelevant details
❌ **Giant Test Cases:** Testing too much in one test

**12. Performance Optimization Checklist:**

✅ Parallel execution configured where safe
✅ Only smoke tests run on every commit
✅ Full regression runs nightly
✅ Data sources limited for quick runs
✅ Assertions ordered by speed
✅ Caching implemented for tokens
✅ Connection pooling enabled
✅ Memory settings optimized
✅ Slow tests identified and optimized
✅ Regular performance reviews

content.title: Managing Test Assets with Version Control
content.explanation:
**Treating Tests as First-Class Code Artifacts:**

Version control is not just for source code—it's essential for managing test assets, enabling collaboration, and maintaining history.

**Why Version Control for Tests Matters:**

```
Without Version Control:
❌ Who changed this test last?
❌ What changed between runs?
❌ How do we collaborate?
❌ How do we roll back a bad change?
❌ Which version matches this API version?

With Version Control:
✅ Full change history
✅ Blame for debugging
✅ Branching for features
✅ Tagging for releases
✅ Collaboration through pull requests
```

**1. What to Version Control:**

```
Repository Structure:
api-tests/
├── projects/
│   ├── user-api.xml
│   ├── product-api.xml
│   └── order-api.xml
├── data/
│   ├── test-users.csv
│   ├── test-products.csv
│   └── test-orders.csv
├── scripts/
│   ├── CommonUtilities.groovy
│   ├── DataGenerators.groovy
│   └── AssertionHelpers.groovy
├── schemas/
│   ├── user-schema.json
│   ├── product-schema.json
│   └── order-schema.xsd
├── config/
│   ├── dev.properties
│   ├── staging.properties
│   └── prod.properties
├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

**2. Git-Friendly Project Structure:**

```xml
<!-- Store properties externally, not in project file -->
<soapui-project name="API Tests">
  <properties>
    <!-- Reference external properties file -->
    <property name="configFile" value="${projectDir}/config/${#System#ENV}.properties"/>
  </properties>
</soapui-project>
```

**3. Environment-Specific Configuration:**

```properties
# dev.properties
api.baseUrl=https://dev-api.example.com
api.key=dev-api-key-123
db.host=localhost
db.name=testdb

# staging.properties
api.baseUrl=https://staging-api.example.com
api.key=staging-api-key-456
db.host=staging-db.example.com
db.name=stagingdb

# prod.properties
api.baseUrl=https://api.example.com
api.key=${#System#PROD_API_KEY}  # From environment
db.host=prod-db.example.com
db.name=proddb
```

**4. .gitignore Configuration:**

```gitignore
# Ignore environment-specific files
*.log
*.swp
*.lock

# Ignore local configuration
local.properties
*.local

# Ignore generated reports
reports/
output/

# Ignore sensitive data
*password*
*secret*
*credential*

# Ignore IDE files
.idea/
*.iml
.classpath
.project
.settings/

# Ignore large binary files
*.pdf
*.zip
*.tar.gz
```

**5. Git Workflow for Tests:**

```bash
# Feature branch workflow
git checkout -b feature/new-api-endpoint
# Add new tests
git add tests/new-endpoint.xml
git commit -m "Add tests for new /v2/users endpoint"
git push origin feature/new-api-endpoint
# Create pull request
# Review and merge

# Tag releases
git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "API version 1.2.3 test suite"
git push --tags

# Rollback if needed
git revert HEAD~2
git push
```

**6. Commit Message Conventions:**

```
# Good commit messages
git commit -m "Add tests for user registration validation"
git commit -m "Update product search assertions to match new schema"
git commit -m "Fix flaky test in order cancellation"
git commit -m "Refactor authentication helper script"

# Include issue numbers
git commit -m "Fix #123: Update user ID extraction logic"

# Bad commit messages
git commit -m "Update tests"
git commit -m "Fix stuff"
git commit -m "Changes"
```

**7. Branching Strategy:**

```
main (production-ready tests)
├── develop (integration branch)
│   ├── feature/user-api-update
│   ├── feature/product-search
│   └── fix/flaky-order-test
└── release/v2.0.0 (release candidate)
    └── hotfix/auth-token-expiry
```

**8. Code Review Checklist for Tests:**

✅ Test names clearly describe purpose
✅ No hardcoded values
✅ Assertions validate business logic
✅ Error cases covered
✅ Test data is appropriate
✅ No duplicate tests
✅ Documentation updated
✅ Performance acceptable
✅ Follows naming conventions
✅ Property usage correct

**9. Continuous Integration with Version Control:**

```yaml
# GitHub Actions workflow
git checkout ${{ github.ref }}
testrunner.sh -Penv=${{ github.ref_name }} -f reports project.xml
```

**10. Version Control Best Practices:**

✅ **Commit Often:** Small, focused commits
✅ **Write Good Messages:** Explain why, not just what
✅ **Branch for Features:** Keep main stable
✅ **Review Changes:** Pull requests for all changes
✅ **Tag Releases:** Link tests to API versions
✅ **Ignore Generated Files:** Don't commit reports
✅ **Store Secrets Securely:** Use environment variables
✅ **Document Setup:** README for new team members

**11. Version Control Anti-Patterns:**

❌ **Large Binary Files:** Don't commit reports or large files
❌ **Hardcoded Paths:** Use relative paths only
❌ **No .gitignore:** Committing temporary files
❌ **Vague Messages:** "Update tests" is not helpful
❌ **Direct Main Commits:** Always use pull requests
❌ **Unreviewed Changes:** No code review for tests
❌ **Outdated Branches:** Stale branches never merged

**12. Version Control Checklist:**

✅ Repository structure defined
✅ .gitignore configured
✅ External properties for environments
✅ README with setup instructions
✅ Commit message conventions
✅ Branch strategy documented
✅ Review process in place
✅ Tags for releases
✅ CI integration configured
✅ Team trained on workflow

content.title: Putting It All Together: A Best Practices Example
content.scenario: Building a well-structured, maintainable test suite
content.outcome: Professional-grade test automation framework
content.details:
**Complete Test Case Following All Best Practices:**

```xml
<testCase name="TC023_Order_Create_ValidData">
  <description>
    Create a new order with valid data and verify all business rules
    
    Preconditions:
    - User must be authenticated (token in project properties)
    - Products must exist in inventory
    
    Test Data:
    - Product IDs: from CSV test-data.csv
    - Quantities: 1-5 per product
    - Shipping address: from test-data.csv
    
    Business Rules:
    - Orders over $1000 require approval
    - Tax rate varies by country
    - Inventory decreases after order
    
    Tags: @regression @order @critical
    Author: QA Team
    Created: 2024-03-15
    Last Updated: 2024-03-30
  </description>
  
  <properties>
    <!-- External configuration -->
    <property name="baseUrl" value="${#Project#apiUrl}"/>
    <property name="authToken" value="${#Project#authToken}"/>
    
    <!-- Test-specific properties with defaults -->
    <property name="orderId" value=""/>
    <property name="createdOrderId" value=""/>
    <property name="expectedTotal" value="0"/>
  </properties>
  
  <setupScript>
    <![CDATA[
      log.info "Starting test: ${testRunner.testCase.name}"
      log.info "Environment: ${context.expand('${#Project#env}')}"
      
      // Verify prerequisites
      assert context.expand('${#Project#authToken}') : "Auth token required"
    ]]>
  </setupScript>
  
  <testSteps>
    <!-- Step 1: Get available products (cached) -->
    <testStep name="Get Products" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${baseUrl}/products?limit=5</endpoint>
        <method>GET</method>
        <headers>
          <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
        </headers>
      </config>
      <assertions>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Count"><path>$</path><expected>5</expected></assertion>
      </assertions>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 2: Extract product IDs for order -->
    <testStep name="Extract Product IDs" type="groovy">
      <script>
        <![CDATA[
          def response = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("Get Products")
              .getPropertyValue("response")
          def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(response)
          
          // Select random products for order
          def selectedProducts = []
          def random = new Random()
          (1..3).each { i ->
            def product = json[random.nextInt(json.size())]
            selectedProducts << [
              productId: product.id,
              quantity: 1 + random.nextInt(3),
              price: product.price
            ]
          }
          
          context.setProperty('orderItems', groovy.json.JsonOutput.toJson(selectedProducts))
          log.info "Selected ${selectedProducts.size()} products for order"
        ]]>
      </script>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 3: Create order with selected products -->
    <testStep name="Create Order" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${baseUrl}/orders</endpoint>
        <method>POST</method>
        <headers>
          <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
          <header name="Content-Type">application/json</header>
        </headers>
        <request>
          <![CDATA[
          {
            "items": ${orderItems},
            "shippingAddress": {
              "country": "US",
              "zipCode": "10001"
            }
          }
          ]]>
        </request>
      </config>
      <assertions>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>201,202</codes></assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.orderId</path></assertion>
        <assertion type="Response SLA"><time>3000</time></assertion>
      </assertions>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 4: Extract order ID -->
    <testStep name="Extract Order ID" type="transfer">
      <transfers>
        <transfer>
          <source type="response" step="Create Order">
            <path>$.orderId</path>
          </source>
          <target type="property">
            <name>createdOrderId</name>
          </target>
        </transfer>
      </transfers>
    </testStep>
    
    <!-- Step 5: Verify order details -->
    <testStep name="Get Order" type="restrequest">
      <config>
        <endpoint>${baseUrl}/orders/${createdOrderId}</endpoint>
        <method>GET</method>
        <headers>
          <header name="Authorization">Bearer ${authToken}</header>
        </headers>
      </config>
      <assertions>
        <assertion type="Valid HTTP Status Codes"><codes>200</codes></assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Match"><path>$.id</path><value>${createdOrderId}</value></assertion>
        <assertion type="JSONPath Existence"><path>$.items</path></assertion>
        <assertion type="Script">
          <script>
            <![CDATA[
              import groovy.json.JsonSlurper
              
              def json = new JsonSlurper().parseText(messageExchange.responseContent)
              def items = json.items
              
              // Business rule: Order total should match items * quantities
              def calculatedTotal = items.sum { it.price * it.quantity }
              assert Math.abs(calculatedTotal - json.total) < 0.01 : 
                  "Total ${json.total} doesn't match calculated ${calculatedTotal}"
              
              log.info "Order verification passed: ID=${json.id}, Total=${json.total}"
            ]]>
          </script>
        </assertion>
      </assertions>
    </testStep>
  </testSteps>
  
  <tearDownScript>
    <![CDATA[
      // Clean up test order
      def orderId = context.getProperty('createdOrderId')
      if (orderId) {
        try {
          def deleteStep = testRunner.testCase.getTestStepByName("Delete Order")
          deleteStep.setPropertyValue('orderId', orderId)
          deleteStep.run(testRunner, context)
          log.info "Cleaned up order ${orderId}"
        } catch (Exception e) {
          log.warn "Cleanup failed: ${e.message}"
        }
      }
      
      // Log test summary
      log.info "=== Test Summary ==="
      log.info "Test: ${testRunner.testCase.name}"
      log.info "Status: ${testRunner.status}"
      log.info "Duration: ${testRunner.timeTaken}ms"
      log.info "Order ID: ${orderId ?: 'N/A'}"
    ]]>
  </tearDownScript>
</testCase>
```

**This test case demonstrates all best practices:**

✅ **Organization:** Clear naming, documentation, tags
✅ **Data Management:** No hardcoding, dynamic product selection
✅ **Dynamic Data:** Property transfers for IDs
✅ **Assertions:** Layered, including business logic
✅ **Performance:** Fast checks first, caching where possible
✅ **Error Handling:** Cleanup, clear messages
✅ **Maintenance:** Properties for configuration
✅ **Documentation:** Detailed description, expectations

By following these best practices, you'll create test suites that are reliable, maintainable, and provide real value to your development process.

Differentiate between JIRA Software, JIRA Service Management, and JIRA Core
Discover the benefits JIRA brings to development teams and organizations
