content.title: Understanding Project Types: Team-Managed vs Company-Managed
content.explanation:
**Choosing the Right Project Governance Model:**

JIRA offers two fundamentally different ways to manage projects. Understanding the difference is crucial for proper setup.

**1. Team-Managed Projects (formerly Next-Gen)**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 Team-Managed Projects                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Designed for: Individual teams that want autonomy              │
│                                                                  │
│  Key Characteristics:                                            │
│  ✓ Team configures their own project                             │
│  ✓ Simpler interface and settings                                │
│  ✓ Predefined workflows that can't be modified                   │
│  ✓ Team members have admin rights by default                     │
│  ✓ No global scheme inheritance                                  │
│  ✓ Faster to set up and use                                      │
│                                                                  │
│  Best for: Small teams, pilot projects, autonomous squads       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**2. Company-Managed Projects (Classic)**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                Company-Managed Projects                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Designed for: Organizations needing consistency and control    │
│                                                                  │
│  Key Characteristics:                                            │
│  ✓ Centralized configuration by JIRA admins                      │
│  ✓ Full workflow customization                                   │
│  ✓ Schemes (permission, notification, etc.) shared across projects│
│  ✓ Fine-grained permission control                               │
│  ✓ Complex configurations possible                               │
│  ✓ Scales across hundreds of projects                            │
│                                                                  │
│  Best for: Large organizations, regulated industries, multi-team│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Comparison Table:**

| Aspect | Team-Managed | Company-Managed |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| **Configuration** | By team | By JIRA admins |
| **Workflow** | Fixed (can't modify) | Fully customizable |
| **Permissions** | Simple (team members) | Complex schemes |
| **Issue Types** | Predefined set | Fully customizable |
| **Fields** | Limited set | Unlimited custom fields |
| **Screens** | Fixed | Fully customizable |
| **Scheme Sharing** | No | Yes (across projects) |
| **Complexity** | Low | High |
| **Setup Time** | Minutes | Hours/days |
| **Best For** | Individual teams | Enterprise |

**When to Choose Team-Managed:**

✅ Small team (<10 people)
✅ Team wants autonomy
✅ Simple workflow (To Do → In Progress → Done)
✅ No complex customizations needed
✅ Pilot project or proof of concept
✅ Team doesn't have JIRA admin access

**When to Choose Company-Managed:**

✅ Large organization with multiple teams
✅ Need consistent workflows across projects
✅ Complex approval processes
✅ Custom issue types and fields required
✅ Regulatory compliance needs
✅ Need to share configurations
✅ Fine-grained permission control needed

**Migration Path:**

```
Team-Managed → Company-Managed:
- Not directly possible
- Must recreate project
- Export data, create new project, import

Company-Managed → Team-Managed:
- Not recommended (lose functionality)
- Only for simplification scenarios
```

content.title: Mastering Project Configuration
content.explanation:
**Deep Dive into Project Settings and Issue Types:**

Once your project is created, you'll need to configure it for your team's specific needs.

**1. Project Settings Overview (Company-Managed)**

```
Project Settings Menu:
├── Details
│   ├── Name, key, lead, avatar
│   └── Description
├── Issue Types
│   ├── Add/remove issue types
│   ├── Configure issue type schemes
│   └── Set default issue type
├── Workflows
│   ├── Assign workflows to issue types
│   └── View workflow diagram
├── Screens
│   ├── Configure screens for each operation
│   ├── Create/edit screen schemes
│   └── Field configuration
├── Fields
│   ├── Custom fields
│   ├── Field configurations
│   └── Field contexts
├── Permissions
│   ├── Permission scheme
│   └── Project role configuration
├── Notifications
│   ├── Notification scheme
│   └── Event notifications
├── Versions
│   └── Manage releases
├── Components
│   └── Define system areas
└── Automation
    └── Project-level automation rules
```

**2. Issue Types Configuration**

Issue types categorize different kinds of work.

**Default Issue Types in Software Projects:**

| Issue Type | Icon | Purpose | Example |
|------------|------|---------|---------|
| **Epic** | 🏆 | Large initiative | "User Authentication" |
| **Story** | 📖 | User-facing feature | "Login with Google" |
| **Task** | ✅ | Technical work | "Set up database schema" |
| **Bug** | 🐛 | Defect | "Login fails with special chars" |
| **Sub-task** | ◀️ | Breakdown of larger issue | "Design login page" |

**Adding Custom Issue Types:**

```
Step-by-step to add custom issue type:

1. Go to Project Settings > Issue Types
2. Click 'Add issue type'
3. Enter:
   - Name: "Technical Debt"
   - Description: "Code quality improvements"
   - Icon: Choose appropriate icon
4. Choose workflow mapping
5. Click 'Add'
```

**3. Issue Type Schemes**

Schemes control which issue types are available in which projects.

```
Scheme: Default Issue Type Scheme
├── Assigned to: Project A, Project B
├── Issue Types:
│   ├── Epic
│   ├── Story
│   ├── Task
│   ├── Bug
│   └── Sub-task
└── Default: Task

Scheme: Support Project Scheme
├── Assigned to: Project C (Service Desk)
├── Issue Types:
│   ├── Incident
│   ├── Service Request
│   ├── Problem
│   └── Change
└── Default: Service Request
```

**4. Custom Fields**

Custom fields capture information specific to your process.

**Creating a Custom Field:**

```
1. Go to Project Settings > Fields
2. Click 'Create custom field'
3. Choose field type:
   - Text (single/multi line)
   - Number
   - Date/Time
   - Select list (single/multi choice)
   - Radio buttons
   - Checkboxes
   - URL
   - User picker
   - etc.
4. Configure field options
5. Add to screens
6. Set context (which projects/issue types)
```

**Common Custom Field Examples:**

| Field Name | Type | Purpose |
|------------|------|---------|
| **Story Points** | Number | Estimation |
| **Sprint** | Sprint picker | Sprint assignment |
| **QA Lead** | User picker | Quality assurance owner |
| **Environment** | Select list | Dev, Staging, Production |
| **Severity** | Select list | Blocker, Critical, Major, Minor |
| **Fix Version** | Version picker | Release assignment |
| **Security Level** | Select list | Confidential, Internal, Public |

**5. Screens and Screen Schemes**

Screens control which fields appear when creating, editing, or viewing issues.

```
Screen: Create Issue Screen
├── Fields shown when creating new issue
│   ├── Summary (required)
│   ├── Description
│   ├── Priority
│   ├── Component/s
│   └── Fix Version/s

Screen: Edit Issue Screen
├── Fields shown when editing
│   ├── All create fields
│   ├── Status
│   ├── Assignee
│   └── Resolution

Screen: View Issue Screen
├── Fields shown when viewing
│   ├── All fields (read-only)
│   └── Activity stream
```

**Screen Scheme Configuration:**

```
Screen Scheme: Default Screen Scheme
├── Operation: Create Issue → Screen: Create Screen
├── Operation: Edit Issue → Screen: Edit Screen
├── Operation: View Issue → Screen: View Screen
└── Applied to: Projects using this scheme
```

**6. Field Configuration**

Field configurations control field behavior (required, hidden, default values).

```
Field Configuration: Default Field Configuration
├── Summary: Required, no default
├── Description: Optional
├── Priority: Required, default = Medium
├── Environment: Hidden
├── Due Date: Optional
└── Story Points: Required for Stories, optional for Tasks
```

**7. Components**

Components represent logical areas of your system.

```
Project: Mobile App
├── Components:
│   ├── Authentication (Lead: @john)
│   ├── Database (Lead: @jane)
│   ├── API (Lead: @bob)
│   ├── UI (Lead: @alice)
│   └── Push Notifications (Lead: @sarah)

Issues can be assigned to multiple components:
"Fix login error" → Components: Authentication, Database
```

**8. Versions**

Versions represent releases.

```
Project: Mobile App
├── Versions:
│   ├── 1.0.0 (Released: 2024-01-15)
│   ├── 1.1.0 (Released: 2024-02-20)
│   ├── 1.2.0 (In Progress, due: 2024-03-30)
│   ├── 2.0.0 (Planned, due: 2024-06-01)
│   └── Backlog (Unreleased, no due date)
```

**9. Best Practices for Project Configuration**

✅ **Start Simple:** Add customizations only when needed
✅ **Consistent Naming:** Use clear, consistent names for fields
✅ **Limit Custom Fields:** Too many fields overwhelm users
✅ **Use Contexts:** Limit custom fields to relevant issue types
✅ **Document Fields:** Explain purpose of custom fields
✅ **Regular Review:** Remove unused fields periodically
✅ **Test Changes:** Verify in test project first

**10. Common Configuration Mistakes**

❌ **Too Many Fields:** 50+ fields on create screen
❌ **Inconsistent Options:** Same field, different options
❌ **No Defaults:** Users always have to select values
❌ **Wrong Field Types:** Text field for date values
❌ **Missing Required Fields:** Critical data not captured
❌ **Overly Complex:** Unnecessary customizations

content.title: Designing Effective Workflows
content.explanation:
**Mastering JIRA's Most Powerful Feature:**

Workflows define how issues move from creation to completion. They're the engine that drives your team's process.

**1. Workflow Anatomy**

```
┌─────────┐    ┌─────────┐    ┌─────────┐    ┌─────────┐
│  To Do  │───▶│In Progress│───▶│In Review│───▶│  Done   │
└─────────┘    └─────────┘    └─────────┘    └─────────┘
     │              │              │              │
   Status        Status         Status         Status

Transitions (arrows):
- "Start Progress" (To Do → In Progress)
- "Stop Progress" (In Progress → To Do)
- "Start Review" (In Progress → In Review)
- "Approve" (In Review → Done)
- "Reject" (In Review → To Do)
```

**2. Workflow Components**

| Component | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **Status** | State of the issue | "In Progress" |
| **Transition** | Movement between statuses | "Start Progress" |
| **Condition** | Who can perform transition | Only assignee |
| **Validator** | Check before allowing transition | Required fields filled |
| **Post Function** | Action after transition | Send email, update field |

**3. Building a Custom Workflow**

```
Step-by-step to create custom workflow:

1. Go to JIRA Administration (⚙️) > Issues > Workflows
2. Click 'Add workflow'
3. Name: "Software Development Workflow"
4. Description: "Standard dev workflow with review"
5. Choose to copy existing or start from scratch
6. Click 'Add'

7. Design workflow in diagram editor:
   - Add statuses: To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done
   - Add transitions between them
   - Configure each transition
   
8. Add conditions:
   - Only assignee can transition from In Progress
   - Only reviewers can transition to Done
   
9. Add validators:
   - Required fields: Description, Component
   - Check for linked issues
   
10. Add post functions:
    - Assign to next person
    - Update resolution
    - Send notification

11. Publish workflow
12. Associate with issue types in project
```

**4. Workflow Example: Bug Lifecycle**

```
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│  Open    │───▶│In Progress│───▶│  Fixed   │───▶│  Closed  │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘
     │              │              │
     │              │              │
     ▼              ▼              ▼
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│Reopened  │◀───│  Cannot  │◀───│  Won't   │
│          │    │Reproduce │    │   Fix    │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘

Transitions:
1. Open → In Progress: "Start Work"
2. In Progress → Fixed: "Mark Fixed"
3. In Progress → Cannot Reproduce: "Can't Reproduce"
4. Fixed → Closed: "Close Issue"
5. Fixed → Reopened: "Reopen" (if still happening)
6. Closed → Reopened: "Reopen"
7. Cannot Reproduce → Closed: "Close"
8. Won't Fix → Closed: "Close"
```

**5. Transition Conditions**

```
// Examples of transition conditions

Condition: Only Assignee
- Only the person assigned to the issue can perform this transition

Condition: Only Reporter
- Only the person who created the issue can perform this transition

Condition: User in Role
- Only users with specific project role can perform this transition

Condition: Issue Field Value
- Transition allowed only if specific field has certain value

Condition: Subtasks Complete
- All subtasks must be done before parent can be closed
```

**6. Validators**

```
// Examples of validators

Validator: Required Fields
- Check that all required fields are filled

Validator: Permission
- Check that user has specific permission

Validator: Date/Time
- Check that date is valid (e.g., end date > start date)

Validator: Linked Issues
- Check that required linked issues exist

Validator: Custom Script
- Groovy script for complex validation
```

**7. Post Functions**

```
// Examples of post functions

Post Function: Update Issue Field
- Automatically set field values

Post Function: Assign to Current User
- Assign issue to person performing transition

Post Function: Create Linked Issue
- Automatically create subtask or related issue

Post Function: Send Email
- Send notification to specified users

Post Function: Trigger Webhook
- Call external system via webhook

Post Function: Update Change History
- Log transition in issue history
```

**8. Workflow Schemes**

Workflow schemes map workflows to issue types.

```
Workflow Scheme: Software Development Scheme
├── Issue Type: Epic → Workflow: Epic Workflow
├── Issue Type: Story → Workflow: Story Workflow
├── Issue Type: Task → Workflow: Task Workflow
├── Issue Type: Bug → Workflow: Bug Workflow
└── Default → Workflow: Simple Workflow

Applied to: All software projects
```

**9. Advanced Workflow Patterns**

**Parallel Reviews:**
```
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│In Progress│───▶│  Peer Review │───▶│  Done    │
└──────────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────┘
                      │
                      ▼
                ┌──────────────┐
                │ QA Approval  │
                └──────────────┘
```

**Approval Workflow:**
```
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│  Draft   │───▶│Submitted │───▶│Approved  │───▶│  Done    │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘
     │              │              │
     ▼              ▼              ▼
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│ Withdrawn│    │ Rejected │    │ Changes  │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    │Required  │
                                └──────────┘
```

**10. Workflow Best Practices**

✅ **Start Simple:** Begin with basic workflow, add complexity as needed
✅ **Name Clearly:** Status names should be intuitive ("In Progress" not "InDev")
✅ **Limit Statuses:** 5-7 statuses maximum, more creates confusion
✅ **Document Transitions:** Explain what each transition does
✅ **Test Thoroughly:** Test workflow in sandbox before deploying
✅ **Train Users:** Explain new workflow to team
✅ **Review Regularly:** Remove unused statuses/transitions

**11. Common Workflow Mistakes**

❌ **Too Many Statuses:** 20+ statuses nobody understands
❌ **Dead Ends:** Statuses with no way out
❌ **Missing Transitions:** Can't get from A to B
❌ **Circular Workflows:** Loops that never end
❌ **No Validation:** Issues move without required data
❌ **Overly Restrictive:** Nobody can move issues
❌ **Ignoring Users:** Workflow doesn't match real process

**12. Workflow Metrics**

| Metric | What It Measures | Target |
|--------|------------------|--------|
| **Time in Status** | How long issues stay in each status | < 2 days |
| **Transition Count** | Average moves per issue | 3-5 |
| **Reopen Rate** | Issues reopened after closure | < 5% |
| **Cycle Time** | Time from start to completion | Depends on team |

content.title: Securing Your JIRA Instance with Proper Permissions
content.explanation:
**Controlling Access to Projects and Features:**

Permissions ensure the right people have the right access to the right information.

**1. Permission Architecture**

```
JIRA Permission Structure:

Global Permissions (System-wide)
└── Project Permissions (Per project)
    ├── Issue Permissions
    ├── Attachments Permissions
    └── Comments Permissions

Users are assigned to:
├── Groups (e.g., jira-developers, jira-admins)
└── Project Roles (e.g., Project Lead, Developer, Viewer)

Permission Schemes map permissions to groups/roles
```

**2. Global Permissions**

Global permissions apply across the entire JIRA instance.

| Permission | Description | Who Should Have It |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|
| **JIRA Administrators** | Full system admin | IT team (2-3 people) |
| **JIRA Users** | Can log in and use JIRA | All users |
| **Create Shared Objects** | Create filters, dashboards | Power users |
| **Bulk Change** | Modify many issues at once | Project leads |
| **Manage Group Filter Subscriptions** | Manage subscriptions | Project leads |

**3. Project Permissions**

Project permissions control what users can do within a project.

| Permission Category | Specific Permissions |
|--------------------|----------------------|
| **Project Access** | Browse Projects, View Development Tools |
| **Issue Operations** | Create Issues, Edit Issues, Delete Issues |
| **Workflow** | Transition Issues, Assign Issues, Resolve Issues |
| **Comments** | Add Comments, Edit All Comments, Delete All Comments |
| **Attachments** | Create Attachments, Delete All Attachments |
| **Time Tracking** | Work On Issues, Delete Own Worklogs |
| **Voting/Watching** | Vote on Issues, Watch Issues |
| **Moderation** | Moderate Comments, Delete Issues |

**4. Project Roles**

Project roles are logical groupings of permissions.

| Role | Typical Members | Permissions |
|------|-----------------|-------------|
| **Project Lead** | Product Manager | Full project control |
| **Developer** | Development team | Create, edit, transition issues |
| **Reviewer** | Senior devs, architects | Review and approve |
| **QA** | Testers | Test and verify |
| **Viewer** | Stakeholders | View only |
| **Reporter** | Anyone who reports bugs | Create issues, limited edit |

**5. Creating a Permission Scheme**

```
Step-by-step to create permission scheme:

1. Go to JIRA Administration > Issues > Permission Schemes
2. Click 'Add Permission Scheme'
3. Name: "Software Team Permissions"
4. Description: "Standard permissions for dev teams"
5. Click 'Add'

6. Configure permissions:
   - Browse Projects → All authenticated users
   - Create Issues → Developers, Reporters
   - Edit Issues → Developers, Project Lead
   - Transition Issues → Developers, QA
   - Close Issues → Project Lead
   - Delete Issues → JIRA Administrators only

7. Add project roles:
   - Click 'Add' next to each permission
   - Select group or project role
   - Click 'Grant'

8. Associate scheme with projects:
   - Go to project settings > Permissions
   - Select your permission scheme
   - Click 'Associate'
```

**6. Example Permission Scheme**

```
Scheme: Default Software Permissions

Project Access:
├── Browse Projects: Anyone in project

Issue Creation:
├── Create Issues: Developers, Reporters

Issue Editing:
├── Edit Issues: Developers, Project Lead
├── Edit Own Issues: Reporters

Issue Deletion:
├── Delete Issues: Project Lead, JIRA Admins

Workflow:
├── Transition Issues: Developers, QA
├── Assign Issues: Developers, Project Lead
├── Resolve Issues: Developers
├── Close Issues: Project Lead, QA

Comments:
├── Add Comments: Anyone in project
├── Edit Own Comments: Anyone
├── Delete Own Comments: Anyone
├── Edit All Comments: Project Lead
├── Delete All Comments: JIRA Admins

Attachments:
├── Create Attachments: Anyone in project
├── Delete Own Attachments: Anyone
├── Delete All Attachments: Project Lead
```

**7. Issue Security Levels**

Issue security restricts access to specific issues.

```
Security Scheme: Confidential Issues
├── Security Level: Public
│   └── Visible to: All users
├── Security Level: Internal
│   └── Visible to: Project team only
├── Security Level: Confidential
│   └── Visible to: Project Lead, Management
├── Security Level: Executive
│   └── Visible to: Executives only

Usage:
When creating an issue, reporter can set security level
Issues with higher security are hidden from most users
```

**8. Best Practices for Permissions**

✅ **Principle of Least Privilege:** Give minimum access needed
✅ **Use Roles, Not Individuals:** Assign permissions to roles
✅ **Default to Viewer:** Start restrictive, add as needed
✅ **Regular Audits:** Review permissions quarterly
✅ **Document Changes:** Track why permissions changed
✅ **Test Permissions:** Verify with test users
✅ **Separate Admins:** Limit number of global admins

**9. Common Permission Mistakes**

❌ **Too Many Admins:** 20 people with admin access
❌ **Overly Permissive:** Everyone can delete anything
❌ **No Viewer Role:** Stakeholders can't see progress
❌ **Individual Permissions:** Managing 100 individual users
❌ **Ignoring Roles:** Not using project roles
❌ **Inconsistent Schemes:** Different perms in each project
❌ **No Review Process:** Anyone can change anything

**10. Permission Testing Checklist**

✅ Can developers create issues?
✅ Can developers edit their own issues?
✅ Can developers transition issues?
✅ Can QA transition to Done?
✅ Can reporters see their issues?
✅ Can stakeholders view the board?
✅ Can't developers delete issues?
✅ Can't viewers edit issues?
✅ Can leads see all issues?
✅ Can admins access everything?

content.title: Keeping Everyone Informed Without Overwhelming Them
content.explanation:
**Configuring Notifications and Automation for Efficient Communication:**

Notifications and automation reduce manual work and keep teams informed.

**1. Notification Architecture**

```
Event (e.g., Issue Created)
    ↓
Notification Scheme
    ↓
Recipients (individuals, groups, roles)
    ↓
Delivery Method (email, Slack, in-app)
```

**2. Notification Events**

JIRA can notify on many events:

| Event Category | Specific Events |
|----------------|-----------------|
| **Issue Creation** | Issue Created |
| **Issue Updates** | Issue Updated, Issue Assigned |
| **Workflow** | Issue Resolved, Issue Closed, Issue Reopened |
| **Comments** | Comment Added, Comment Edited, Comment Deleted |
| **Attachments** | Attachment Added, Attachment Removed |
| **Work Log** | Work Logged, Work Log Updated |
| **Watchers** | Watcher Added, Watcher Removed |
| **Sprints** | Sprint Started, Sprint Ended |
| **Versions** | Version Released |

**3. Creating a Notification Scheme**

```
Step-by-step to create notification scheme:

1. Go to JIRA Administration > Issues > Notification Schemes
2. Click 'Add Notification Scheme'
3. Name: "Standard Team Notifications"
4. Description: "Default notifications for dev teams"
5. Click 'Add'

6. Configure notifications:
   - Issue Created → Project Lead, Current Assignee
   - Issue Assigned → New Assignee
   - Issue Resolved → Reporter, Watchers
   - Issue Closed → Reporter, Watchers
   - Comment Added → Watchers

7. Associate with projects:
   - Go to project settings > Notifications
   - Select your notification scheme
   - Click 'Associate'
```

**4. Example Notification Scheme**

```
Scheme: Development Team Notifications

Issue Created:
├── Project Lead
├── Component Lead
└── Watchers

Issue Updated:
├── Assignee
└── Watchers

Issue Assigned:
├── New Assignee
└── Reporter

Issue Resolved:
├── Reporter
├── Watchers
└── QA Team

Issue Reopened:
├── Assignee
├── Reporter
└── Watchers

Comment Added:
├── Assignee
├── Reporter
└── Watchers

Work Logged:
├── Project Lead
└── Watchers
```

**5. Automation Rules**

Automation rules automate repetitive tasks without code.

**Rule Components:**

```
When: [Trigger] (e.g., Issue Created)
If: [Condition] (e.g., Priority = High)
Then: [Action] (e.g., Assign to lead, notify team)
```

**Common Automation Examples:**

```
Rule 1: Auto-assign Critical Bugs
When: Issue Created
If: Issue Type = Bug AND Priority = Critical
Then: Assign to Project Lead, Add label "critical", Send Slack notification

Rule 2: Move Done Issues
When: Sprint Ends
If: Status = Done
Then: Move to next sprint

Rule 3: Remind of Due Dates
When: Daily at 9 AM
If: Due Date < 2 days AND Status != Done
Then: Send email to assignee

Rule 4: Auto-close Resolved Issues
When: Status = Resolved
If: Resolution = Fixed AND 7 days passed
Then: Transition to Closed
```

**6. Creating Automation Rules**

```
Step-by-step (JIRA Cloud):

1. Go to Project Settings > Automation
2. Click 'Create rule'
3. Choose trigger:
   - Issue event (created, updated, etc.)
   - Scheduled (time-based)
   - Manual trigger
4. Add conditions (optional)
5. Add branch (optional, for multiple issues)
6. Add actions:
   - Edit issue fields
   - Transition issue
   - Create issue
   - Send email
   - Send web request
   - Add comment
7. Test rule
8. Turn on rule
```

**7. Email Notifications Configuration**

```
Configure email server:

1. Go to JIRA Administration > System > Mail
2. Add outgoing mail server:
   - Name: "Company SMTP"
   - Protocol: SMTP
   - Host: smtp.company.com
   - Port: 587
   - TLS: Yes
   - Username: notifications@company.com
   - Password: (secure password)
3. Test connection
4. Set as default

Configure email notifications:
5. Go to user profile > Notification settings
6. Users can customize their preferences
```

**8. Slack Integration**

```
Integrate JIRA with Slack:

1. Install JIRA Cloud app from Slack App Directory
2. Connect JIRA to Slack workspace
3. Configure channel subscriptions:
   - /jira subscribe [project] [channel]
   - e.g., /jira subscribe MOB #mobile-dev
4. Choose events to notify
5. Get notifications in Slack
```

**9. Best Practices for Notifications**

✅ **Right Information, Right People:** Not too many, not too few
✅ **Use @mentions Sparingly:** Don't over-notify
✅ **Let Users Customize:** Allow notification preferences
✅ **Test Before Deploying:** Verify who gets what
✅ **Review Regularly:** Remove noisy notifications
✅ **Use Automation Wisely:** Don't automate everything
✅ **Document Rules:** Explain what automation does

**10. Common Notification Mistakes**

❌ **Too Many Emails:** 50+ emails per day
❌ **Wrong Recipients:** Sending to whole company
❌ **Noisy Automations:** Bot comments on every issue
❌ **Missing Important Alerts:** Critical issues ignored
❌ **No User Control:** Users can't mute notifications
❌ **Email Overload:** People start ignoring emails
❌ **Complex Rules:** Nobody understands the automation

**11. Automation Use Cases by Role**

| Role | Helpful Automations |
|------|---------------------|
| **Developer** | Auto-assign based on component, remind of due dates |
| **QA** | Auto-create test tasks, notify when ready for testing |
| **PM** | Auto-update epics when stories complete, release notes |
| **Support** | Auto-respond to tickets, escalate unresolved issues |
| **Everyone** | Daily summary of work, mention when mentioned |

**12. Metrics to Track**

| Metric | What It Measures | Target |
|--------|------------------|--------|
| **Notifications per User** | Email volume | < 10/day |
| **Automation Success Rate** | Rules working correctly | > 99% |
| **Manual Actions Saved** | Hours saved by automation | 10+ hours/week |
| **Response Time** | Time to first response | < 4 hours |
| **User Satisfaction** | Survey results | > 4/5 |

content.title: Connecting JIRA to Your Development Toolchain
content.explanation:
**Building a Connected Ecosystem for End-to-End Traceability:**

JIRA becomes truly powerful when integrated with the tools your team already uses.

**1. Integration Architecture**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         JIRA                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Code → GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket                                  │
│  Build → Jenkins/CircleCI/Bamboo                                 │
│  Deploy → AWS/Azure/Heroku                                       │
│  Monitor → Sentry/Datadog/New Relic                              │
│  Test → TestRail/Zephyr/Xray                                     │
│  Docs → Confluence                                               │
│  Chat → Slack/Microsoft Teams                                    │
│  Design → Figma/InVision                                         │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**2. GitHub Integration**

```
Setup GitHub Integration:

1. Install JIRA Cloud app from GitHub Marketplace
2. Connect JIRA to GitHub organization
3. Configure repositories to sync
4. Set up smart commits:

   Commit message format:
   PROJ-123 #comment Fixed login bug
   PROJ-123 #time 2h Spent 2 hours debugging
   PROJ-123 #close Issue resolved

   JIRA automatically:
   - Links commits to issues
   - Updates issue status
   - Logs work time
   - Shows PRs in issue view
```

**Benefits:**

- **Traceability:** Code changes linked to requirements
- **Automation:** Auto-transition issues on commit
- **Visibility:** See PRs in issue view
- **Context:** Developers see issue details in IDE

**3. Jenkins Integration**

```
Setup Jenkins Integration:

1. Install JIRA Plugin in Jenkins
2. Configure JIRA connection
3. In Jenkins jobs:
   - Add JIRA environment variables
   - Add post-build actions to update JIRA

Example Jenkins Pipeline:
```groovy
stage('Build') {
    steps {
        echo 'Building...'
    }
    post {
        success {
            jiraIssueUpdate(
                idOrKey: "PROJ-123",
                transition: "In Review",
                comment: "Build successful"
            )
        }
        failure {
            jiraIssueUpdate(
                idOrKey: "PROJ-123",
                transition: "Failed",
                comment: "Build failed"
            )
        }
    }
}
```
```

**Benefits:**

- **Build Status:** See build results in JIRA
- **Auto-Transition:** Move issues based on build results
- **Deployment Tracking:** Link builds to versions

**4. Slack Integration**

```
Setup Slack Integration:

1. Install JIRA Cloud app from Slack App Directory
2. Connect JIRA to Slack workspace
3. Configure notifications:

   /jira subscribe PROJ #project-channel
   /jira subscribe all #general

Receive notifications:
- New issues created
- Status changes
- Mentions
- Custom alerts

Interactive features:
- Create issues from Slack
- View issue details
- Comment on issues
- Transition issues
```

**Benefits:**

- **Real-time updates:** Instant notifications
- **Reduced context switching:** Stay in Slack
- **Collaboration:** Discuss issues in channels

**5. Confluence Integration**

```
Setup Confluence Integration:

1. Both JIRA and Confluence from Atlassian
2. Application links automatically configured
3. Features:

   - Insert JIRA issues in Confluence pages
   - Create release notes from JIRA versions
   - Link documentation to issues
   - View issue details in Confluence
   - Create JIRA issues from Confluence

Example: Release Notes Page

{jiraissues:url=https://company.atlassian.net/issues/?jql=project=PROJ%20AND%20fixVersion=1.2.0}

Displays all issues fixed in version 1.2.0
```

**Benefits:**

- **Documentation:** Requirements linked to documentation
- **Release Notes:** Auto-generate from issues
- **Knowledge Base:** Link solutions to issues

**6. TestRail Integration**

```
Setup TestRail Integration:

1. Install TestRail JIRA add-on
2. Configure connection
3. Features:

   - Link test cases to JIRA issues
   - Create JIRA bugs from failed tests
   - See test results in JIRA
   - Auto-update test status

TestRail → JIRA:
When a test fails, automatically create bug with:
- Test case details
- Environment info
- Steps to reproduce
- Screenshots

JIRA → TestRail:
When bug is fixed, update test case status
```

**Benefits:**

- **Quality Tracking:** Tests linked to requirements
- **Automated Bug Creation:** No manual entry
- **Traceability:** From bug to test

**7. Custom Webhooks**

```
Setup Webhook Integration:

1. Go to JIRA Administration > System > Webhooks
2. Create new webhook:
   - Name: "Notify External System"
   - URL: https://api.example.com/jira-webhook
   - Events: Issue created, updated, deleted
   - JQL filter: project = PROJ

Webhook payload (JSON):
{
  "event": "issue_updated",
  "issue": {
    "key": "PROJ-123",
    "summary": "Fix login bug",
    "status": "In Progress",
    "assignee": "john.doe"
  },
  "user": "jane.smith",
  "timestamp": "2024-03-12T10:30:00Z"
}
```

**Benefits:**

- **Custom Integration:** Connect any system
- **Real-time Sync:** Instant updates
- **Flexible:** Customize payload

**8. Integration Best Practices**

✅ **Start Small:** Integrate one tool at a time
✅ **Test Thoroughly:** Verify integration works
✅ **Document Setup:** Keep integration documentation
✅ **Monitor Performance:** Watch for slowdowns
✅ **Security First:** Use API tokens, not passwords
✅ **Regular Updates:** Keep plugins updated
✅ **Train Team:** Show how to use integrations

**9. Common Integration Mistakes**

❌ **Too Many Notifications:** Every commit notifies everyone
❌ **Broken Links:** Outdated application links
❌ **Security Gaps:** Hardcoded credentials
❌ **Performance Issues:** Too many webhooks
❌ **No Error Handling:** Integrations fail silently
❌ **Untested Changes:** Breaking integrations with upgrades
❌ **Ignoring Rate Limits:** API limits exceeded

**10. Integration Checklist**

✅ Code repository (GitHub/GitLab) connected
✅ CI/CD (Jenkins) integrated
✅ Team chat (Slack) connected
✅ Documentation (Confluence) linked
✅ Testing tools integrated
✅ Monitoring tools connected
✅ Custom webhooks configured
✅ Authentication secured
✅ Notifications tuned
✅ Team trained

content.scenario: Setting up JIRA for a new mobile app development team
content.outcome: Fully configured JIRA instance ready for development
content.details:
**Team Profile:**
- 8 developers, 2 QA, 1 product manager
- Building iOS and Android apps
- Using Scrum with 2-week sprints
- GitHub for code, Jenkins for CI, Slack for chat

**Step 1: Choose Deployment**

```
Decision: JIRA Cloud
Reason: Small team, no IT staff, quick setup

Created site: mobileteam.atlassian.net
Added 11 users (8 dev, 2 QA, 1 PM)
Selected JIRA Software (Standard plan)
```

**Step 2: Create Projects**

```
Project 1: iOS App
- Name: "iOS Mobile App"
- Key: IOS
- Template: Scrum software development
- Lead: iOS Tech Lead

Project 2: Android App
- Name: "Android Mobile App"
- Key: AND
- Template: Scrum software development
- Lead: Android Tech Lead

Shared Components:
- Authentication
- Database
- API
- UI
- Push Notifications
```

**Step 3: Configure Issue Types**

```
Added custom issue types:
- Technical Debt (for refactoring)
- Performance Issue (for optimization)

Custom fields:
- Story Points (number)
- Platform (iOS/Android/Both)
- App Version (version picker)
- QA Lead (user picker)

Screen configurations:
- Added Story Points to create screen for Stories
- Added Platform field to all issues
- Made App Version required for Bugs
```

**Step 4: Customize Workflows**

```
Created custom workflow: Mobile Dev Workflow

Statuses:
1. To Do
2. In Progress
3. Code Review
4. QA Testing
5. Done

Transitions:
- Start Progress (To Do → In Progress)
  → Condition: Assignee set
  → Post-function: Assign to current user

- Request Review (In Progress → Code Review)
  → Validator: All fields filled
  → Post-function: Notify reviewers

- Approve (Code Review → QA Testing)
  → Condition: Reviewer in role
  → Post-function: Assign to QA

- Reject (Code Review → In Progress)
  → Post-function: Add comment, reassign

- Start Testing (QA Testing → In Progress) if fails
- Pass Testing (QA Testing → Done)
  → Post-function: Set resolution = Fixed
```

**Step 5: Set Up Permissions**

```
Created permission scheme: Mobile Team Permissions

Project Roles:
- Project Lead (PM and tech leads)
- Developer (8 developers)
- QA (2 testers)
- Reviewer (senior devs)
- Viewer (stakeholders)

Permissions:
- Browse Projects: All roles
- Create Issues: Developer, QA
- Edit Issues: Developer, QA, Lead
- Transition Issues: Developer, QA, Reviewer
- Delete Issues: Lead only
- Add Comments: All roles
- Create Attachments: All roles
- Resolve Issues: Developer
- Close Issues: QA, Lead
```

**Step 6: Configure Notifications**

```
Notification scheme: Mobile Team Notifications

Events → Recipients:
- Issue Created: Project Lead, Watchers
- Issue Assigned: New Assignee
- Issue Resolved: Reporter, QA
- Issue Reopened: Assignee, Reporter
- Comment Added: Watchers
- Code Review Requested: Reviewers
- QA Testing Started: QA Team

Users can customize email preferences
```

**Step 7: Create Automation Rules**

```
Rule 1: Auto-assign Bugs by Component
When: Issue Created
If: Issue Type = Bug AND Component = "Authentication"
Then: Assign to auth-team@company.com, Add label "auth"

Rule 2: Daily Standup Reminder
When: Every weekday at 9:30 AM
If: Status != Done
Then: Send Slack reminder to #mobile-dev

Rule 3: Sprint Cleanup
When: Sprint Ends
If: Status = Done
Then: Transition to Closed

Rule 4: Escalate Stalled Issues
When: Status = In Progress > 5 days
Then: Notify Project Lead, Add label "stalled"
```

**Step 8: Set Up Integrations**

```
GitHub Integration:
- Connected mobileteam org
- Smart commits enabled
- Commit format: IOS-123 #comment #time #close

Jenkins Integration:
- Added JIRA plugin
- Build jobs update issue status
- Test results linked to issues

Slack Integration:
- Subscribed to #mobile-dev
- Notifications for status changes
- /jira command to create issues

Confluence Integration:
- Linked space for documentation
- Auto-generated release notes
```

**Step 9: Create Initial Backlog**

```
Epics:
1. User Authentication
2. Profile Management
3. Push Notifications
4. Offline Mode

Stories (sample):
- IOS-101: Implement login screen
- IOS-102: Add Google Sign-in
- IOS-103: Implement biometric login
- AND-101: Design Android login UI
- AND-102: Implement auth API client

Bugs (sample):
- IOS-201: Login crashes on iPhone 12
- AND-202: Memory leak in profile view
```

**Step 10: Plan First Sprint**

```
Sprint 1: Authentication Foundation
Duration: March 10-24, 2024
Goal: Implement basic authentication

Selected issues (32 story points):
- IOS-101: Login screen (5 points)
- IOS-102: Google Sign-in (3 points)
- IOS-103: Biometric login (8 points)
- AND-101: Android login UI (5 points)
- AND-102: Auth API client (8 points)
- AND-103: Session management (3 points)

Team capacity: 40 points
Ready to start development!
```

**Results:**

✅ Fully configured JIRA instance
✅ Team onboarded and trained
✅ All tools integrated
✅ First sprint planned
✅ Automation saving time
✅ Clear visibility for everyone

This setup provides the team with everything they need to start developing efficiently with complete traceability and automation.

content.title: How JIRA Supports Agile Methodologies
content.explanation:
**Understanding JIRA's Agile Capabilities:**

JIRA was originally a bug tracker, but it has evolved into the world's most popular tool for Agile teams. Its flexibility allows it to support Scrum, Kanban, and hybrid approaches.

**The Agile Spectrum in JIRA:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Agile Methodologies in JIRA                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Scrum                    Kanban                    Scrumban    │
│  ┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐│
│  │ Fixed sprints   │     │ Continuous flow │     │ Hybrid      ││
│  │ Time-boxed      │     │ WIP limits      │     │ Sprints +   ││
│  │ Cross-functional│     │ Pull-based      │     │ WIP limits  ││
│  │ teams           │     │ Flow metrics    │     │             ││
│  └─────────────────┘     └─────────────────┘     └─────────────┘│
│                                                                  │
│  JIRA Boards adapt to your methodology, not the other way around│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key Agile Concepts in JIRA:**

| Concept | JIRA Implementation | Purpose |
|---------|---------------------|---------|
| **Epic** | Large body of work spanning multiple sprints | Track major initiatives |
| **Story** | User-facing feature | Capture requirements from user perspective |
| **Task** | Technical work item | Track implementation work |
| **Bug** | Defect or problem | Track issues and fixes |
| **Sprint** | Time-boxed iteration (Scrum) | Deliver work in regular cadence |
| **Board** | Visual representation of work | See status, manage flow |
| **Backlog** | Prioritized list of future work | Plan and prioritize |
| **WIP Limit** | Maximum items in a column (Kanban) | Prevent bottlenecks |

**JIRA's Agile Philosophy:**

```
Visibility: All work visible to everyone
Collaboration: Teams work together seamlessly
Inspection: Regular reviews of progress
Adaptation: Continuous improvement based on data
Transparency: No hidden work or status
```

**Getting Started with Agile in JIRA:**

```
Step 1: Choose your methodology (Scrum or Kanban)
Step 2: Create a project with the appropriate template
Step 3: Configure your board
Step 4: Add your team
Step 5: Create your backlog
Step 6: Start your first sprint or start pulling work
Step 7: Inspect and adapt using JIRA's reports
```

content.title: Mastering Scrum with JIRA
content.explanation:
**Using Scrum Boards to Manage Time-Boxed Iterations:**

Scrum is about delivering value in fixed-length iterations called sprints. JIRA's Scrum boards make this process visual and manageable.

**Scrum Board Anatomy:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Sprint: Sprint 12 (March 10-24, 2024)                          │
│  Goal: Implement user authentication and profile management     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  To Do (5)    │ In Progress (3) │ In Review (2) │ Done (8)    │
├───────────────┼─────────────────┼───────────────┼─────────────┤
│ AUTH-101      │ AUTH-105        │ AUTH-108      │ AUTH-100    │
│ AUTH-102      │ AUTH-106        │ AUTH-109      │ AUTH-103    │
│ AUTH-104      │ AUTH-107        │               │ AUTH-110    │
│ AUTH-111      │                 │               │ AUTH-112    │
│ AUTH-113      │                 │               │ AUTH-114    │
└───────────────┴─────────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────┘

Quick Filters:
[My Issues] [Reported by Me] [Done] [High Priority]
```

**Setting Up a Scrum Board:**

```
Step-by-step to create a Scrum board:

1. Create a new project with "Scrum software development" template
   OR
   Go to Boards > Create Board > Scrum board

2. Select project(s) to include
3. Name your board (e.g., "Mobile App Scrum Board")
4. Configure columns to match your workflow:
   - To Do
   - In Progress
   - In Review
   - Done

5. Set column mapping to issue statuses:
   - To Do → To Do, Open
   - In Progress → In Progress
   - In Review → In Review
   - Done → Done, Closed

6. Configure quick filters for common views
7. Add swimlanes if needed (by assignee, priority, etc.)
```

**Scrum Board Features:**

| Feature | Description | How to Use |
|---------|-------------|------------|
| **Sprint** | Time-boxed iteration | Create, start, complete sprints |
| **Backlog** | Future work | Prioritize, estimate, drag to sprint |
| **Active Sprint** | Current work | Update status, track progress |
| **Swimlanes** | Group issues | By assignee, priority, epic |
| **Quick Filters** | Filter view | Show only my issues, high priority |
| **Card Colors** | Visual cues | Color by priority, issue type |
| **Drag & Drop** | Move issues | Update status, reorder |

**Sprint Lifecycle in JIRA:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Sprint Lifecycle                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  1. Create Sprint: Name it, set dates                           │
│          ↓                                                       │
│  2. Add Issues: Drag from backlog to sprint                     │
│          ↓                                                       │
│  3. Start Sprint: Team begins work                              │
│          ↓                                                       │
│  4. Daily Updates: Move cards, update status                    │
│          ↓                                                       │
│  5. Complete Sprint: Review completed work                      │
│          ↓                                                       │
│  6. Sprint Report: Review metrics, plan next                    │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Swimlanes Example:**

```
Swimlane by Assignee:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ John's Issues                                                    │
├───────────────┬─────────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┤
│ AUTH-101      │ AUTH-105        │ AUTH-108      │ AUTH-100      │
└───────────────┴─────────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Jane's Issues                                                    │
├───────────────┬─────────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┤
│ AUTH-102      │ AUTH-106        │ AUTH-109      │ AUTH-103      │
└───────────────┴─────────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Bob's Issues                                                     │
├───────────────┬─────────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┤
│ AUTH-104      │ AUTH-107        │               │ AUTH-104      │
└───────────────┴─────────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────┘
```

**Best Practices for Scrum Boards:**

✅ **Keep Columns Simple:** 3-5 columns maximum
✅ **Update Daily:** Board should reflect reality
✅ **Limit Work in Progress:** Don't start too much
✅ **Use Swimlanes Wisely:** Only if they add value
✅ **Celebrate Progress:** Watch cards move to Done
✅ **Review at Standup:** Walk the board each day
✅ **Sprint Goal Visible:** Display prominently

**Common Scrum Board Mistakes:**

❌ **Too Many Columns:** Confusing, hard to manage
❌ **Stale Board:** Status not updated
❌ **No WIP Limits:** Too much work started
❌ **Missing Swimlanes:** Can't see assignments
❌ **Ignoring Blockers:** Cards stuck for days
❌ **Scope Creep:** Adding work mid-sprint
❌ **No Sprint Goal:** Team doesn't know purpose

content.title: Keeping Your Backlog Healthy and Prioritized
content.explanation:
**The Art of Backlog Management:**

The backlog is the single source of truth for all future work. A well-groomed backlog is essential for effective sprint planning.

**Backlog Structure:**

```
Backlog View
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Epic: User Authentication
├── ▶ AUTH-101: Implement login screen (5 points)
├── ▶ AUTH-102: Add Google Sign-in (3 points)
├── ▶ AUTH-103: Implement biometric login (8 points)
└── ▶ AUTH-104: Password reset flow (5 points)

Epic: Profile Management
├── ▶ PRO-101: User profile screen (3 points)
├── ▶ PRO-102: Edit profile functionality (5 points)
└── ▶ PRO-103: Avatar upload (2 points)

Epic: Push Notifications
├── ▶ NOT-101: Notification settings (3 points)
├── ▶ NOT-102: Push service integration (8 points)
└── ▶ NOT-103: Notification history (5 points)

Epic: Offline Mode
├── ▶ OFF-101: Local data storage (8 points)
└── ▶ OFF-102: Sync when online (5 points)
```

**Prioritization Techniques in JIRA:**

| Technique | How JIRA Supports | Best For |
|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| **MoSCoW** | Priority field (Must, Should, Could, Won't) | Feature prioritization |
| **WSJF** | Custom fields for business value, time criticality | SAFe, scaled agile |
| **Value vs Effort** | Story points + custom value field | ROI-based decisions |
| **Stack Ranking** | Drag and drop ordering | Simple prioritization |
| **Kano Model** | Labels or custom fields | Customer satisfaction |

**Backlog Grooming Activities:**

```
Regular Grooming Tasks:

1. Review new issues (add to backlog, assign priority)
2. Estimate unestimated stories (assign story points)
3. Split large stories into smaller ones
4. Remove or deprecate outdated issues
5. Reorder based on changing priorities
6. Add acceptance criteria to stories
7. Link related issues
8. Assign components and labels
```

**Estimation with Story Points:**

```
Story Points Guide:
1 point  = Very simple (1-2 hours)
2 points = Simple (half day)
3 points = Medium (1 day)
5 points = Complex (2-3 days)
8 points = Very complex (3-5 days)
13 points = Too large (needs splitting)

Team's velocity: Average points completed per sprint

Fibonacci sequence (1,2,3,5,8,13) prevents over-thinking
```

**Setting Up Estimation in JIRA:**

```
1. Create custom field "Story Points" (Number field)
2. Add to Scrum project screens
3. Team agrees on estimation scale
4. Estimate during backlog grooming
5. JIRA automatically calculates velocity
```

**Backlog Filters and Views:**

```jql
// Find unestimated stories
project = MOB AND issuetype = Story AND "Story Points" is EMPTY

// Find high priority items
project = MOB AND priority in (Highest, High) AND status != Done

// Find items for next sprint
project = MOB AND status != Done ORDER BY Rank ASC

// Find epics without stories
project = MOB AND issuetype = Epic AND issue NOT IN linkedIssues()
```

**Backlog Grooming Best Practices:**

✅ **Groom Weekly:** 30-60 minutes per week
✅ **Top of Backlog Ready:** Top items ready for next sprint
✅ **Estimated Stories:** All stories have points
✅ **Clear Acceptance Criteria:** Everyone knows "done"
✅ **Dependencies Identified:** Blockers visible
✅ **Remove Dead Items:** Don't keep stale issues
✅ **Business Value Visible:** Priority clear

**Common Backlog Mistakes:**

❌ **Backlog Too Long:** Hundreds of items, never reviewed
❌ **No Estimates:** Can't plan sprints
❌ **Vague Stories:** No acceptance criteria
❌ **Wrong Priorities:** Old items still at top
❌ **Dependency Hell:** No visibility of blockers
❌ **Giant Stories:** 13+ point stories never split
❌ **Stale Backlog:** Never groomed, full of outdated items

**Backlog Grooming Checklist:**

✅ All top 20 items reviewed
✅ All stories in top 10 estimated
✅ Acceptance criteria clear
✅ Dependencies identified
✅ Priority matches business needs
✅ No 13+ point stories (split if needed)
✅ Epics have child stories
✅ Labels and components assigned
✅ Links to related issues

content.title: From Planning to Delivery: Running Successful Sprints
content.explanation:
**Making Sprints Effective with JIRA:**

Sprint planning is where the team commits to work for the next iteration. JIRA makes this process collaborative and data-driven.

**Sprint Planning in JIRA:**

```
Sprint Planning View
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Sprint: Sprint 13 (March 24 - April 7, 2024)
Team Velocity: 42 points (last 3 sprints average)

Backlog (45 points available)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Drag items to sprint:

[ ] AUTH-105: Implement 2FA (5 pts) ← in sprint
[ ] AUTH-106: Session management (3 pts) ← in sprint
[ ] PRO-101: User profile screen (3 pts) ← in sprint
[ ] PRO-102: Edit profile (5 pts) ← in sprint
[ ] NOT-101: Notification settings (3 pts) ← in sprint

Sprint total: 35 points (within capacity ✓)

Add 5 more points:
[ ] NOT-102: Push service (8 pts) → exceeds capacity
[ ] OFF-101: Local storage (8 pts) → exceeds capacity
[ ] AUTH-107: Password rules (3 pts) ← recommended

Sprint Goal: "Complete authentication features and basic profile"
```

**Sprint Planning Steps:**

```
1. Review velocity (how much can we do?)
2. Discuss priorities (what's most important?)
3. Select stories from backlog (drag to sprint)
4. Break down stories into tasks (optional)
5. Set sprint goal (single sentence)
6. Team commits to the work
7. Start sprint
```

**Capacity Planning:**

```
Team: 5 developers × 10 days = 50 person-days
Vacation: 2 devs × 2 days = 4 person-days lost
Training: 1 dev × 2 days = 2 person-days lost

Effective capacity: 50 - 4 - 2 = 44 person-days

Story point to day ratio: 1 point ≈ 1 person-day
Target sprint points: 40-44 points (buffer for unknowns)
```

**During the Sprint:**

**Daily Standup View:**

```
Active Sprint Board
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Yesterday I Did:
- John: Completed AUTH-105, started AUTH-106
- Jane: Fixed AUTH-108, code review
- Bob: Working on AUTH-107

Today I Will Do:
- John: Finish AUTH-106, start AUTH-109
- Jane: Complete AUTH-108 review, start testing
- Bob: Continue AUTH-107, help with blockers

Blockers:
- AUTH-110 blocked by API team (need endpoint)
```

**Managing Sprint Progress:**

```
Sprint Progress Indicators:

1. Remaining work (burndown chart)
   - Tracks if you're on schedule
   - Updates automatically as issues resolve

2. Blocked issues (flagged)
   - Red flags indicate impediments
   - Scrum master helps resolve

3. Scope changes (added/removed)
   - Track mid-sprint changes
   - Discuss at daily standup

4. Team capacity (remaining hours)
   - Log work daily
   - Adjust if behind/ahead
```

**Ending the Sprint:**

```
Sprint Completion Process:

1. Ensure all "Done" issues are in Done column
2. Review incomplete work
3. Generate Sprint Report
4. Demo completed work
5. Retrospective
6. Close sprint

JIRA automatically:
- Moves incomplete issues back to backlog
- Calculates sprint metrics
- Updates velocity
- Creates release notes
```

**Handling Incomplete Work:**

```
Options for incomplete issues:

1. Move back to backlog (default)
   - Re-estimate if needed
   - Prioritize for next sprint

2. Move to next sprint
   - If sprint immediately follows
   - Team commits to completing

3. Split and carry over
   - Complete what's done
   - Move remainder to backlog
```

**Sprint Planning Best Practices:**

✅ **Use Historical Velocity:** Base on data, not guesses
✅ **Leave Buffer:** 10-15% capacity for unknowns
✅ **Clear Sprint Goal:** One sentence, team aligned
✅ **Break Down Tasks:** Stories into manageable tasks
✅ **Check Dependencies:** Don't start blocked work
✅ **Team Commits:** Everyone agrees, not just told
✅ **Review Capacity:** Account for time off, meetings

**Common Sprint Planning Mistakes:**

❌ **Overcommitting:** 120% of capacity
❌ **No Sprint Goal:** Just random work
❌ **Ignoring Velocity:** Guessing instead of using data
❌ **No Buffer:** Any issue derails sprint
❌ **Dependency Ignored:** Blocked from day one
❌ **Top-Down Commitment:** Team told what to do
❌ **Forgetting Time Off:** Vacation not accounted for

**Sprint Execution Checklist:**

✅ Daily standup held
✅ Board updated
✅ Blockers flagged
✅ Work logged
✅ Progress tracked
✅ Scope changes managed
✅ Communication active
✅ Team focused on sprint goal

content.title: Mastering Kanban with JIRA
content.explanation:
**Using Kanban for Continuous Flow Without Sprints:**

Kanban is about visualizing work, limiting work in progress, and maximizing flow. It's ideal for teams with continuous, unpredictable work like support, operations, or maintenance.

**Kanban Board Anatomy:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Kanban Board                                 │
├──────────┬────────────┬──────────────┬────────┬─────────┬───────┤
│ Backlog  │ Selected   │ In Progress  │ Review │ Testing │ Done  │
│ (No WIP) │ (WIP: 3)   │ (WIP: 2)     │(WIP:2) │(WIP:2)  │(No WIP)│
├──────────┼────────────┼──────────────┼────────┼─────────┼───────┤
│ Item 1   │ Item 4     │ Item 6 ◊     │ Item 8 │ Item 10 │ Item12│
│ Item 2   │ Item 5     │ Item 7 ◊     │ Item 9 │         │ Item13│
│ Item 3   │            │              │        │         │ Item14│
│ Item 4   │            │              │        │         │       │
│ Item 5   │            │              │        │         │       │
└──────────┴────────────┴──────────────┴────────┴─────────┴───────┘
◊ = Currently being worked on
WIP limits shown in parentheses
```

**Setting Up a Kanban Board:**

```
Step-by-step to create a Kanban board:

1. Create a new project with "Kanban software development" template
   OR
   Go to Boards > Create Board > Kanban board

2. Select project(s) to include
3. Name your board (e.g., "Support Kanban Board")
4. Configure columns to match your workflow:
   - Backlog
   - Selected for Development
   - In Progress
   - In Review
   - Testing
   - Done

5. Set WIP limits for each column:
   - Selected: 3
   - In Progress: 2 per person
   - In Review: 3
   - Testing: 3

6. Map columns to issue statuses
7. Configure quick filters
```

**WIP Limits in Action:**

```
How WIP limits work:

When a column reaches its limit:
- Cannot pull more work into that column
- Must finish something first
- Visual indicator (red) shows blocked column

Example:
In Progress (WIP: 2)
- Item A (John)
- Item B (Jane)

Team member finishes Item A, moves to Review
In Progress now has 1 item
Can pull new work from Selected
```

**WIP Limit Strategies:**

| Strategy | Description | Example |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| **Per Person** | Limit per team member | WIP: 2 per person |
| **Per Column** | Total limit for column | In Progress: 5 total |
| **Per Role** | Different limits by role | Devs: 2, QA: 3 |
| **Progressive** | Tighter limits downstream | Dev: 5, Test: 3, Deploy: 1 |

**Kanban Metrics:**

| Metric | Definition | Target |
|--------|------------|--------|
| **Lead Time** | Time from request to delivery | < 5 days |
| **Cycle Time** | Time from start to finish | < 3 days |
| **Throughput** | Items completed per week | 10-15 |
| **WIP** | Work in progress | 2-3 per person |
| **CFD** | Cumulative Flow Diagram | No bottlenecks |

**Cumulative Flow Diagram (CFD) Explained:**

```
Cumulative Flow Diagram
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 80 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 70 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 60 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 50 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 40 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 30 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 20 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 10 │   ######················································   │
│    │   ######················································   │
│ 0  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────   │
│      W1   W2   W3   W4   W5   W6   W7   W8   W9   W10          │
│                                                                  │
│  Legend: ███ To Do   ███ In Progress   ███ Done                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Reading the CFD:
- Gap between lines shows WIP
- Slope shows throughput
- Flat lines indicate bottlenecks
- Widening gaps = problems
```

**Kanban vs Scrum Decision Guide:**

| Factor | Choose Kanban | Choose Scrum |
|--------|---------------|--------------|
| **Work Type** | Continuous, unpredictable | Project-based, predictable |
| **Team** | Support, Ops, Maintenance | Development, Product |
| **Delivery** | As soon as ready | Fixed iterations |
| **Planning** | On-demand | Sprint planning |
| **Metrics** | Lead time, cycle time | Velocity, burndown |
| **Changes** | Can reprioritize anytime | Fixed during sprint |
| **Best For** | Support, bug fixes | Features, projects |

**Kanban Best Practices:**

✅ **Visualize Everything:** All work on the board
✅ **Start Where You Are:** Don't change process overnight
✅ **Respect WIP Limits:** They're rules, not suggestions
✅ **Measure Flow:** Track lead and cycle time
✅ **Identify Bottlenecks:** Use CFD to find problems
✅ **Limit Meetings:** Kanban needs fewer ceremonies
✅ **Continuous Improvement:** Regular retrospectives

**Common Kanban Mistakes:**

❌ **No WIP Limits:** Just another to-do list
❌ **Too Many Columns:** Confusing, hard to manage
❌ **Ignoring Blockers:** Items stuck for weeks
❌ **No Metrics:** Can't improve without data
❌ **Scrum with Kanban Board:** Still doing sprints
❌ **Unlimited Backlog:** Never pruned or prioritized
❌ **Missing Classes of Service:** All items treated same

**Metrics Best Practices:**

✅ **Use Data, Not Gut Feel:** Let metrics guide decisions

✅ **Act on Insights:** Don't just collect data

**Common Metrics Mistakes:**

**Month 3: Optimization**

```
Week 9-10: Sprint 4

- Velocity stabilizing

Week 11-12: Sprint 5
- Integrated with GitHub

- Completed: 27 points (96%)

Metric            Month 1    Month 2    Month 3    Change

**Key Learnings:**

Before JIRA:
❌ Unknown status until last minute

❌ Stakeholder complaints
❌ Low morale

After JIRA:

✅ Everyone aligned

content.title: What Are JIRA Automation Rules?
content.explanation:
**Automating Repetitive Tasks Without Code:**

JIRA Automation is a powerful no-code tool that allows you to automate repetitive tasks, enforce processes, and reduce manual work. It's like having a virtual assistant that works 24/7 to keep your projects running smoothly.

**The Automation Philosophy:**

```
Manual Work                Automated Work
    │                           │
    ▼                           ▼
❌ Assign issues manually   ✓ Auto-assign by component
❌ Send status emails       ✓ Auto-notify on status change
❌ Update fields            ✓ Auto-calculate and update
❌ Create subtasks          ✓ Auto-create from templates
❌ Move between projects    ✓ Auto-transition workflows
❌ Flag blockers            ✓ Auto-detect and flag
```

**What Can You Automate?**

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Issue Management** | Auto-assign, auto-transition, auto-close |
| **Notifications** | Email, Slack, Microsoft Teams |
| **Field Updates** | Calculate dates, copy values, set defaults |
| **Issue Creation** | Create linked issues, subtasks |
| **Workflow** | Move issues, resolve, reopen |
| **Integrations** | Webhooks, external APIs |
| **Scheduling** | Daily reminders, recurring tasks |

**The ROI of Automation:**

```
Time Savings Calculation:

Manual task: 2 minutes per issue
Issues per week: 100
Time per week: 200 minutes = 3.3 hours

Automation saves: 3 hours/week × 50 weeks = 150 hours/year
Value at $50/hour = $7,500 per year per process

Typical team with 10 automations saves $75,000/year!
```

**Automation Availability:**

| JIRA Edition | Automation Rules | Limits |
|--------------|------------------|--------|
| **JIRA Free** | ✓ 100 rules/month | Basic features |
| **JIRA Standard** | ✓ 500 rules/month | Full features |
| **JIRA Premium** | ✓ 1000+ rules/month | Advanced + branching |
| **JIRA Enterprise** | ✓ Custom limits | Enterprise features |
| **JIRA Server/DC** | ✓ Unlimited | Via add-ons |

**Automation Architecture:**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Automation Rule                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  WHEN [Trigger] happens                                         │
│       ↓                                                         │
│  IF [Conditions] are met                                        │
│       ↓                                                         │
│  THEN [Actions] are performed                                   │
│                                                                  │
│  Optional: BRANCH for each matching item                        │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

content.title: Understanding Automation Components
content.explanation:
**The Building Blocks of Every Automation Rule:**

Every automation rule has three essential components: a trigger, optional conditions, and one or more actions.

**1. Triggers - What Starts the Rule**

Triggers are events that cause the rule to execute.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       TRIGGER TYPES                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Issue Events                                                   │
│  ├── Issue Created                                              │
│  ├── Issue Updated                                               │
│  ├── Issue Deleted                                               │
│  ├── Issue Transitioned                                          │
│  ├── Comment Added                                               │
│  ├── Attachment Added                                            │
│  └── Work Logged                                                 │
│                                                                  │
│  Scheduled                                                       │
│  ├── Daily at specific time                                      │
│  ├── Weekly on specific day                                      │
│  ├── Monthly on specific date                                    │
│  └── Custom interval (cron)                                      │
│                                                                  │
│  Manual                                                          │
│  ├── Run rule now (button)                                       │
│  └── Bulk execution                                              │
│                                                                  │
│  External                                                        │
│  ├── Webhook received                                            │
│  └── API call                                                    │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Trigger Examples:**

```
// Issue Events
When: Issue Created
When: Issue Transitioned from "In Progress" to "Done"
When: Comment Added containing "URGENT"

// Scheduled
When: Every weekday at 9:00 AM
When: First day of every month

// Manual
When: User clicks "Notify Team" button
```

**2. Conditions - Filtering When Rules Run**

Conditions restrict when the rule executes.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      CONDITION TYPES                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Field Conditions                                               │
│  ├── Issue Type equals Bug                                      │
│  ├── Priority equals Critical                                   │
│  ├── Status not equals Done                                     │
│  ├── Due Date is before today                                   │
│  └── Assignee is empty                                          │
│                                                                  │
│  User Conditions                                                │
│  ├── Current user is in group "Managers"                        │
│  ├── Current user is project lead                               │
│  └── Issue reporter is same as current user                     │
│                                                                  │
│  Issue Conditions                                               │
│  ├── Issue has subtasks                                         │
│  ├── Issue is linked to another                                 │
│  ├── Issue has attachments                                      │
│  └── Issue has been updated in last 7 days                      │
│                                                                  │
│  AND/OR Conditions                                              │
│  ├── All conditions must match (AND)                            │
│  └── Any condition can match (OR)                               │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Condition Examples:**

```
// Simple condition
IF: Priority = Critical

// Multiple conditions (AND)
IF: Issue Type = Bug AND Priority = High AND Component = Authentication

// Multiple conditions (OR)
IF: Status = Done OR Resolution = Fixed

// Complex condition
IF: (Priority = Critical OR Priority = Blocker) AND (Due Date < now())
```

**3. Actions - What the Rule Does**

Actions are the operations performed when the rule runs.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        ACTION TYPES                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Issue Operations                                               │
│  ├── Edit issue fields                                          │
│  ├── Transition issue (change status)                           │
│  ├── Assign issue                                               │
│  ├── Add comment                                                 │
│  ├── Add attachment                                              │
│  ├── Link issues                                                 │
│  └── Create issue                                                │
│                                                                  │
│  Notifications                                                  │
│  ├── Send email                                                  │
│  ├── Send Slack message                                          │
│  ├── Send Microsoft Teams message                                │
│  └── Send webhook                                                │
│                                                                  │
│  Workflow                                                       │
│  ├── Transition issue                                            │
│  ├── Resolve issue                                               │
│  ├── Close issue                                                 │
│  └── Reopen issue                                                │
│                                                                  │
│  Project Operations                                             │
│  ├── Create version                                              │
│  ├── Release version                                             │
│  └── Archive version                                             │
│                                                                  │
│  Advanced                                                       │
│  ├── Run Groovy script (Server/DC)                              │
│  ├── Send REST request                                           │
│  └── Log something                                               │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Action Examples:**

```
// Edit field
THEN: Set Priority to High

// Transition
THEN: Transition issue to "In Progress"

// Assign
THEN: Assign to Project Lead

// Notify
THEN: Send email to Reporter

// Multiple actions
THEN: 
  1. Transition to "In Review"
  2. Assign to "reviewers" group
  3. Add comment "Ready for review"
  4. Send Slack notification to #reviews
```

**4. Branches - Working with Multiple Issues**

Branches allow you to perform actions on related issues.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        BRANCH TYPES                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Branch on: Subtasks                                            │
│  └── For each subtask, perform actions                          │
│                                                                  │
│  Branch on: Linked Issues                                       │
│  ├── For each issue linked as "blocks"                          │
│  └── For each issue linked as "relates to"                      │
│                                                                  │
│  Branch on: JQL Query                                           │
│  └── For each issue matching JQL, perform actions               │
│                                                                  │
│  Branch on: Components                                          │
│  └── For each component, perform actions                        │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Branch Example:**

```
WHEN: Issue marked as Done
IF: Issue has subtasks
BRANCH on subtasks:
    IF: Subtask status != Done
    THEN: 
        - Add comment: "Parent completed, please finish this subtask"
        - Set priority to High
```
